translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 118
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 118

sentences.zh: 【晉紀四十】起強圉大荒落，盡屠維協洽，凡三年。

translations.literal: [Jin Records 40], from qiángyù dàhuāngluò through túwéi xiéqià, three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Records 40], spanning from the year qiángyù dàhuāngluò through túwéi xiéqià—a period of three years.

sentences.zh: 安皇帝癸義熙十三年（

translations.literal: The thirteenth year of Yixi of Emperor An, guǐ (
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Yixi during the reign of Emperor An (

sentences.zh: 丁巳，公元四一七年）

translations.literal: dingsi, corresponding to 417 CE)
translations.idiomatic: dingsi, the year 417 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲戌朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on the first day of the month (jiaxu), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month (jiaxu), a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 秦主泓朝會百官於前殿，以內外危迫，君臣相泣。

translations.literal: The Qin ruler Hong held court with the hundred officials in the front hall; because of danger within and without, ruler and ministers wept together.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Hong of Qin assembled his officials in the front hall; with peril pressing at home and abroad, ruler and ministers wept together.

sentences.zh: 征北將軍齊公恢帥安定鎮戶三萬八千，焚廬舍，自北雍州趨長安，自稱大都督、建義大將軍，移檄州郡，欲除君側之惡；

translations.literal: The Campaigning-North General, Duke of Qi Hui, led thirty-eight thousand households of the Anding garrison, burned their dwellings, marched from Northern Yong Province toward Chang'an, styled himself Grand Commander and General-in-Chief Who Establishes Righteousness, and issued a proclamation to the provinces and commanderies, intending to remove evil at the ruler's side;
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning-North General, Duke of Qi Hui, led thirty-eight thousand Anding garrison households, burned their homes, marched from Northern Yong Province toward Chang'an, and proclaimed himself Grand Commander and General-in-Chief Who Establishes Righteousness. He sent proclamations through the provinces and commanderies, declaring his intent to purge evil from the ruler's side;

sentences.zh: 揚威將軍姜紀帥從歸之，建節將軍彭完都棄陰密奔還長安。

translations.literal: the Displaying-Might General Jiang Ji led his followers to join him, and the Establishing-Banner General Peng Wandu abandoned Yinmi and fled back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Displaying-Might General Jiang Ji brought his followers to join him, while Establishing-Banner General Peng Wandu abandoned Yinmi and fled back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 恢至新支，姜紀說恢曰：「國家重將、大兵皆在東方，京師空虛，公亟引輕兵襲之，必克。

translations.literal: When Hui reached Xinzhi, Jiang Ji said to Hui: "The state's weighty generals and great armies are all in the east; the capital is empty. If you quickly lead light troops to strike it, you will surely take it.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui reached Xinzhi, Jiang Ji urged him: "The empire's chief generals and main forces are all in the east, and the capital stands nearly empty. Lead light troops in a swift strike and you are sure to take it.

sentences.zh: 」恢不從，南攻郿城。

translations.literal: " Hui did not follow this advice and instead marched south to attack Mei.
translations.idiomatic: " Hui refused and marched south to attack Mei.

sentences.zh: 鎮西將軍姚諶為恢所敗，長安大震。

translations.literal: The Pacifying-West General Yao Chen was defeated by Hui, and Chang'an was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying-West General Yao Chen was defeated by Hui, throwing Chang'an into alarm.

sentences.zh: 泓馳使征東平公紹，遣姚裕及輔國將軍胡翼度屯澧西。

translations.literal: Hong urgently sent messengers to summon the Duke of the East, Ping Shao, and dispatched Yao Yu and the Assisting-the-State General Hu Yidu to encamp west of the Li.
translations.idiomatic: Hong urgently summoned Duke of the East Ping Shao and sent Yao Yu and Assisting-the-State General Hu Yidu to camp west of the Li River.

sentences.zh: 扶風太守姚俊等皆降於恢。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Fufeng, Yao Jun, and others all surrendered to Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Fufeng Administrator Yao Jun and others all surrendered to Hui.

sentences.zh: 東平公紹引諸軍西還，與恢相持於靈台，姚贊留寧朔將軍尹雅為弘農太守，守潼關，亦引兵還。

translations.literal: The Duke of the East, Ping Shao, led the armies back west and faced Hui at Lingtai; Yao Zan left the Pacifying-the-North General Yin Ya as Administrator of Hongnong to hold Tong Pass and also withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of the East Ping Shao led the armies west to face Hui at Lingtai. Yao Zan left Pacifying-the-North General Yin Ya as Administrator of Hongnong to hold Tong Pass and withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 恢眾見諸軍四集，皆有懼心，其將齊黃等詣大軍降。

translations.literal: Hui's host, seeing the armies gathering on all sides, were all afraid; his generals Qi Huang and others went to the main army and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui's men saw armies converging from every quarter, fear spread through the ranks; his generals Qi Huang and others went over to the main army and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 恢進兵副紹，贊自後擊之，恢兵大敗，殺恢及其三弟。

translations.literal: Hui advanced to press Shao; Zan struck from the rear, and Hui's army was utterly defeated; Hui and his three younger brothers were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Hui pressed forward against Shao; Zan attacked from the rear and routed him. Hui and his three younger brothers were killed.

sentences.zh: 泓器之慟，葬以公禮。

translations.literal: Hong esteemed him and grieved; he was buried with the rites due a duke.
translations.idiomatic: Hong held him in esteem and mourned deeply, burying him with ducal honors.

sentences.zh: 太尉裕引水軍發彭城，留其子彭城公義隆鎮彭城。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Liu Yu led the water army out from Pengcheng and left his son, the Prince of Pengcheng Yilong, to hold Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Liu Yu led the fleet out from Pengcheng, leaving his son, Prince of Pengcheng Yilong, to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 詔以義隆為監徐、兗、青、冀四州諸軍事、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Yilong Supervisor of Military Affairs for Xu, Yan, Qing, and Ji provinces and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Yilong supervisor of military affairs for Xu, Yan, Qing, and Ji and Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 涼公暠寢疾，遣命長史宋繇曰：「吾死之後，世子猶卿子也，善訓導之。

translations.literal: The Lord of Liang Gao took to his bed with illness and left instructions to the Chief Clerk Song Yao: "After my death, the heir is still as your son; train and guide him well.
translations.idiomatic: Lord of Liang Gao fell gravely ill and charged Chief Clerk Song Yao: "After I am gone, treat the heir as you would your own son and guide him well.

sentences.zh: 」二月，暠卒，官屬奉世子歆為大都督、大將軍、涼公、領涼州牧。

translations.literal: " In the second month Gao died; the officials installed the heir Xin as Grand Commander, Grand General, Lord of Liang, and Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: " In the second month Gao died, and his officials installed the heir Xin as Grand Commander, Grand General, Lord of Liang, and Governor of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元嘉興。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was declared, and the era name was changed to Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed to Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 尊歆母天水尹氏為太后。

translations.literal: Xin's mother, the Yin clan of Tianshui, was honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's mother, Lady Yin of Tianshui, was honored as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 以宋繇錄三府事。

translations.literal: Song Yao was put in charge of the affairs of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yao was placed in charge of the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 謚暠曰武昭王，廟號太祖。

translations.literal: Gao was given the posthumous title King Wuzhao, with the temple name Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was posthumously titled King Wuzhao, with the temple name Taizu.

sentences.zh: 西秦安東將軍木弈干擊吐谷渾樹洛干，破其弟阿柴於堯桿川，俘五千餘口而還。

translations.literal: The Pacifying-the-East General of Western Qin, Muyigan, attacked Tuyuhun's Murong Shuluogan, defeated his younger brother Achai at Yao'gan River, captured more than five thousand people, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Western Qin's Pacifying-the-East General Muyigan attacked Tuyuhun's Murong Shuluogan, defeated his younger brother Achai on the Yao'gan River, took more than five thousand captives, and returned.

sentences.zh: 樹洛干走保白蘭山，慚憤發疾，將卒，謂阿柴曰：「吾子拾虔幼弱，今以大事付汝。

translations.literal: Shuluogan fled to hold Mount Bailan; ashamed and enraged, he fell ill; as he was about to die he said to Achai: "My son Sheqian is young and weak; I now entrust the great affair to you.
translations.idiomatic: Shuluogan fled to Mount Bailan. Ashamed and furious, he fell ill; on his deathbed he told Achai: "My son Sheqian is still young; I entrust the great matter to you.

sentences.zh: 」樹洛干卒，阿柴立，自稱驃騎將軍、沙州刺史。

translations.literal: " Shuluogan died; Achai was installed and styled himself General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Shazhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Shuluogan died. Achai succeeded him, styling himself General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Shazhou.

sentences.zh: 謚樹洛干曰武王。

translations.literal: Shuluogan was given the posthumous title King Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Shuluogan was posthumously titled King Wu.

sentences.zh: 阿柴稍用兵侵並其傍小種，地方數千里，遂為強國。

translations.literal: Achai gradually used troops to invade and absorb the small tribes around him; his territory reached several thousand li and he became a powerful state.
translations.idiomatic: Achai gradually used force to absorb neighboring tribes until his domain stretched thousands of li, making Tuyuhun a power to be reckoned with.

sentences.zh: 河西王蒙遜遣其將襲烏啼部，大破之；

translations.literal: The King of Hexi, Mengxun, sent his general to raid the Wuti tribe and inflicted a great defeat;
translations.idiomatic: King of Hexi Mengxun sent a general to strike the Wuti tribe and routed them;

sentences.zh: 又擊卑和部，降之。

translations.literal: he also attacked the Beihe tribe and made them submit.
translations.idiomatic: then attacked the Beihe tribe and brought them to submission.

sentences.zh: 王鎮惡進軍澠池，遣毛德祖襲尹雅於蠡吾城，禽之，雅殺守者而逃。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen'e advanced to Mianchi and sent Mao Dezu to strike Yin Ya at Liwu city; Yin was captured, but he killed the guards and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e advanced on Mianchi and sent Mao Dezu to seize Yin Ya at Liwu; Yin was taken but killed his guards and escaped.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡引兵徑前，抵潼關。

translations.literal: Zhen'e led his troops straight forward and reached Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e pressed straight on to Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 檀道濟、沈林子自陝北渡河，拔襄邑堡，秦河北太守薛帛奔河東。

translations.literal: Tan Daoji and Shen Linzi crossed the river from north of Shan, took Xiangyi fort, and the Qin Administrator of Hebei, Xue Bo, fled to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji and Shen Linzi crossed from north of Shan, took Xiangyi fort, and Qin's Administrator of Hebei, Xue Bo, fled to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 又攻秦并州刺史尹昭於蒲阪，不克。

translations.literal: They also attacked the Qin Inspector of Bing Province, Yin Zhao, at Puban but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: They also attacked Qin Inspector of Bing Yin Zhao at Puban but failed to take the city.

sentences.zh: 別將攻匈奴堡，為姚成都所敗。

translations.literal: A separate detachment attacked the Xiongnu fort and was defeated by Yao Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: A detached force attacked the Xiongnu fort and was beaten by Yao Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，滎陽守將傅洪以虎牢降魏。

translations.literal: On xinyou, the defending general of Xingyang, Fu Hong, surrendered Hulao to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Xingyang's defender Fu Hong surrendered Hulao to Wei.

sentences.zh: 秦主泓以東平公紹為太宰、大將軍、都督中外諸軍事，假黃鉞，改封魯公，使督武衛將軍姚鸞等步騎五萬守潼關，又遣別將姚驢救蒲阪。

translations.literal: The Qin ruler Hong appointed the Duke of the East, Ping Shao, as Grand Preceptor, Grand General, and Commander of All Military Affairs Within and Without, with the yellow battle-axe conferred, changed his fief to Duke of Lu, and sent him to command the Martial Guard General Yao Luan and others with fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to hold Tong Pass; he also sent a separate general, Yao Lü, to relieve Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Hong of Qin made Duke of the East Ping Shao Grand Preceptor and Grand General, commander of all forces within and without, with the yellow battle-axe conferred, changed his title to Duke of Lu, and sent him with Martial Guard General Yao Luan and fifty thousand foot and horse to hold Tong Pass. He also dispatched General Yao Lü to relieve Puban.

sentences.zh: 沈林子謂檀道濟曰：「蒲阪城堅兵多，不可猝拔，攻之傷眾，守之引日。

translations.literal: Shen Linzi said to Tan Daoji: "Puban is a strong city with many troops; it cannot be taken in a rush. To attack it will harm our forces; to besiege it will drag on for days.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Linzi told Tan Daoji: "Puban is strong and well manned—it cannot be rushed. An assault will cost us dearly; a siege will drag on.

sentences.zh: 王鎮惡在潼關，勢孤力弱，不如與鎮惡合勢並力，以爭潼關。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen'e is at Tong Pass, isolated and weak; it would be better to join forces with Zhen'e and combine strength to contest Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e at Tong Pass stands isolated and outmatched. Better to join him and throw our combined weight at the pass.

sentences.zh: 若得之，尹昭不攻自潰矣。

translations.literal: If we take it, Yin Zhao will collapse without being attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Take the pass, and Yin Zhao at Puban will collapse without a fight.

sentences.zh: 」道濟從之。

translations.literal: " Daoji followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Daoji agreed.

sentences.zh: 三月，道濟、林子至潼關，秦魯公紹引兵出戰，道濟、林子奮擊，大破之，斬獲以千數。

translations.literal: In the third month Daoji and Linzi reached Tong Pass; the Qin Duke of Lu, Shao, led his troops out to fight; Daoji and Linzi struck fiercely and inflicted a great defeat, killing and capturing by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Daoji and Linzi reached Tong Pass. Duke of Lu Shao came out to fight; they struck hard and routed him, killing and capturing thousands.

sentences.zh: 紹退屯定城，據險拒守，謂諸將曰：「道濟等兵力不多，懸軍深入，不過堅壁以待繼援。

translations.literal: Shao withdrew to encamp at Dingcheng, holding the dangerous ground and refusing battle, and said to his generals: "Daoji and the others do not have many troops; they have marched deep with a detached force and can do no more than hold their walls and wait for reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Shao fell back to Dingcheng, holding the heights and refusing battle. He told his generals: "Daoji's force is small—they have marched deep and can only sit behind their walls waiting for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 吾分軍絕其糧道，可坐禽也。

translations.literal: If we divide our army and cut off their grain route, we can take them sitting down.
translations.idiomatic: Split our forces and cut their supply line, and we can take them without a fight.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣姚鸞屯大路以絕道濟糧道。

translations.literal: " He then sent Yao Luan to encamp on the Great Road to cut off Daoji's supply line.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Yao Luan to hold the Great Road and sever Daoji's supplies.

sentences.zh: 鸞遣尹雅將兵與晉戰於關南，為晉兵所獲，將殺之。

translations.literal: Luan sent Yin Ya to lead troops to fight the Jin south of the pass; Yin was captured by Jin troops and was about to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Luan sent Yin Ya to fight the Jin south of the pass. Yin was captured and was about to be executed.

sentences.zh: 雅曰：「雅前日已當死，幸得脫至今，死固甘心。

translations.literal: Yin said: "I ought to have died the other day; it was my fortune to escape until now, and death I accept willingly.
translations.idiomatic: Yin said: "I should have died before; it was fortune that let me escape until now, and I accept death willingly.

sentences.zh: 然夷、夏雖殊，君臣之義一也。

translations.literal: Yet though barbarian and Chinese differ, the righteousness between ruler and minister is one.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though barbarian and Chinese differ, the bond between ruler and minister is the same.

sentences.zh: 晉以大義行師，獨不使秦有守節之臣乎！

translations.literal: The Jin march on great principle—will you alone deny Qin a minister who holds to his duty?
translations.idiomatic: The Jin march on righteous principle—will you deny Qin even one minister who keeps faith?

sentences.zh: 」乃免之。

translations.literal: " He was then spared.
translations.idiomatic: " He was spared.

sentences.zh: 丙子夜，沈林子將銳卒襲鸞營，斬鸞，殺其士卒數千人。

translations.literal: On the night of bingzi, Shen Linzi led picked troops in a night raid on Luan's camp, beheaded Luan, and killed several thousand of his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of bingzi, Shen Linzi led picked troops in a night raid on Luan's camp, killed him, and cut down several thousand of his men.

sentences.zh: 紹又遣東平公贊屯河上以斷水道；

translations.literal: Shao also sent the Duke of the East, Ping Zan, to encamp on the river to cut the water route;
translations.idiomatic: Shao also sent Duke of the East Ping Zan to hold the river and cut their water supply;

sentences.zh: 沈林子擊之，贊敗走，還定城。

translations.literal: Shen Linzi attacked him; Zan was defeated and fled, returning to Dingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Linzi attacked and routed him; Zan fled back to Dingcheng.

sentences.zh: 薛帛據河曲來降。

translations.literal: Xue Bo, holding the bend of the river, came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Bo, holding the river bend, came over to the Jin.

sentences.zh: 太尉裕將水軍自淮、泗入清河，將溯河西上，先遣使假道於魏；

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Liu Yu was to lead the water army from the Huai and Si into the Qing River and then go up the Yellow River westward; he first sent envoys to request passage through Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Liu Yu was to lead the fleet from the Huai and Si into the Qing River and up the Yellow River westward. He first sent envoys to request passage through Wei;

sentences.zh: 秦主泓亦遣使請救於魏。

translations.literal: the Qin ruler Hong also sent envoys to ask Wei for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: while Lord Hong of Qin also sent envoys to plead for Wei's aid.

sentences.zh: 魏主嗣使群臣議之，皆曰：「潼關天險，劉裕以水軍攻之，甚難；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler Si had his ministers discuss it; all said: "Tong Pass is a heavenly barrier; for Liu Yu to attack it with a water army would be very difficult;
translations.idiomatic: Wei ruler Si convened his ministers. All said: "Tong Pass is a natural fortress; Liu Yu would find it very hard to take it by river;

sentences.zh: 若登岸北侵，其勢便易。

translations.literal: if he lands on the north bank and invades northward, his position becomes easy.
translations.idiomatic: but if he lands on the north bank and strikes north, his position becomes far easier.

sentences.zh: 裕聲言伐秦，其志難測。

translations.literal: Yu proclaims he is attacking Qin, but his intent is hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: Yu claims he marches against Qin, yet his true aim is hard to read.

sentences.zh: 且秦，婚姻之國，不可不救也。

translations.literal: Moreover Qin is a state joined to us by marriage; we cannot fail to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Qin is tied to us by marriage—we cannot refuse to help.

sentences.zh: 宜發兵斷河上流，勿使得西。

translations.literal: We should send troops to block the upper reaches of the river and not let him go west.
translations.idiomatic: We should send troops to block the upper river and keep him from going west.

sentences.zh: 」博士祭酒崔浩曰：「裕圖秦久矣。

translations.literal: " The Libationer of the Erudites Cui Hao said: "Yu has long plotted against Qin.
translations.idiomatic: " Libationer of the Erudites Cui Hao said: "Yu has long coveted Qin.

sentences.zh: 今姚興死，子泓懦劣，國多內難。

translations.literal: Now Yao Xing is dead, his son Hong is weak and inferior, and the state has many internal troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing is dead; his son Hong is timid and weak, and the realm is torn by internal strife.

sentences.zh: 裕乘其危而伐之，其志必取。

translations.literal: Yu takes advantage of its peril to attack; his aim is surely to conquer.
translations.idiomatic: Yu strikes while Qin is in peril—he means to conquer it.

sentences.zh: 若遏其上流，裕心忿戾，必上岸北侵，是我代秦受敵也。

translations.literal: If we block his upstream passage, Yu's heart will grow resentful and he will surely land on the north bank and invade north—we would be taking Qin's enemies upon ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Block his passage upstream and Yu, enraged, will surely land north and strike us—we would be fighting Qin's war for them.

sentences.zh: 今柔然寇邊，民食又乏，若復與裕為敵，發兵南赴則北寇愈深，救北則南州復危，非良計也。

translations.literal: Now Rouran raids the borders and the people's food is scarce; if we again make an enemy of Yu, sending troops south will let the northern raiders go deeper, and saving the north will leave the southern provinces in danger again—this is not a good plan.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran raids our borders and food runs short. Make an enemy of Yu as well, and if we march south the northern raiders will press deeper; save the north and the south falls into peril again. That is no good plan.

sentences.zh: 不若假之水道，聽裕西上，然後屯兵以塞其東。

translations.literal: It would be better to lend him the water route, let Yu go west, and then station troops to block his east.
translations.idiomatic: Better to grant him the river, let Yu go west, then mass troops to block his retreat eastward.

sentences.zh: 使裕克捷，必德我之假道；

translations.literal: If Yu wins, he will surely be grateful for our lending the route;
translations.idiomatic: If Yu wins, he will owe us for the passage;

sentences.zh: 不捷，吾不失救秦之名。

translations.literal: if he does not win, we lose nothing of the name of having aided Qin.
translations.idiomatic: if he fails, we still keep the name of having aided Qin.

sentences.zh: 此策之得者也。

translations.literal: This is the strategy that gains.
translations.idiomatic: That is the winning strategy.

sentences.zh: 且南北異俗，借使國家棄恆山以南，裕必不能以吳、越之兵與吾爭守河北之地，安能為吾患乎！

translations.literal: Moreover north and south have different customs; even if the state abandoned everything south of Mount Heng, Yu surely could not use Wu and Yue troops to contest with us for holding the lands north of the Yellow River—how could he become our trouble!
translations.idiomatic: North and south differ in custom. Even if we lost everything south of Mount Heng, Yu could not use Wu and Yue troops to contest Hebei with us—how would he threaten us?

sentences.zh: 夫為國計者，惟社稷是利，豈顧一女子乎！

translations.literal: Those who plan for a state look only to what profits the altars of soil and grain—why care for one woman!
translations.idiomatic: Statesmen weigh only the altars of soil and grain—why fret over one woman!

sentences.zh: 」議者猶曰：「裕西入關，則恐吾斷其後，腹背受敵；

translations.literal: " The debaters still said: "If Yu enters the passes westward, he will fear that we cut off his rear and be attacked front and back;
translations.idiomatic: " Others still argued: "If Yu enters the passes west, he will fear we cut his rear and trap him between two fires;

sentences.zh: 北上，則姚氏必不出關助我，其勢必聲西而實北也。

translations.literal: if he goes north, the Yao clan will surely not come out of the passes to aid us—his thrust will surely feign west while striking north in fact.
translations.idiomatic: if he turns north, the Yao will not leave the passes to help us—he will feint west while striking north in truth.

sentences.zh: 」嗣乃以司徒長孫嵩督山東諸軍事，又遣振威將軍娥清、冀州刺史阿薄干將步騎十萬屯河北岸。

translations.literal: " Si thereupon put the Minister of Education Changsun Song in charge of military affairs east of the mountains, and also sent the Displaying-Might General E Qing and the Inspector of Ji Province A Bogan to lead one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry to encamp on the north bank of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: " Si then put Minister of Education Changsun Song in charge of forces east of the mountains and sent Displaying-Might General E Qing and Inspector of Ji A Bogan with one hundred thousand foot and horse to camp on the north bank of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，裕引軍入河，以左將軍向彌為北青州刺史，留戍碻磝。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Yu led his army into the river, appointed the General of the Left Xiang Mi as Inspector of Northern Qing Province, and left him to garrison Que'ao.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Yu entered the river, made General of the Left Xiang Mi Inspector of Northern Qing, and left him to garrison Que'ao.

sentences.zh: 初，裕命王鎮惡等：「若克洛陽，須大軍到俱進。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yu had ordered Wang Zhen'e and the others: "If you take Luoyang, you must wait for the main army to arrive and advance together.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Yu had ordered Wang Zhen'e and the others: "If you take Luoyang, wait for the main army before advancing together.

sentences.zh: 」鎮惡等乘利徑趨潼關，為秦兵所拒，不得前。

translations.literal: " Zhen'e and the others, seizing the advantage, pressed straight for Tong Pass but were blocked by Qin troops and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhen'e and the others pressed straight for Tong Pass on the momentum of victory but were blocked by Qin troops and could not get through.

sentences.zh: 久之，乏食，眾心疑懼，或欲棄輜重還赴大軍。

translations.literal: After a long time food ran short; hearts in the army grew doubtful and afraid, and some wished to abandon the baggage train and return to join the main army.
translations.idiomatic: Food ran short; doubt and fear spread through the ranks, and some wanted to abandon the baggage train and rejoin the main force.

sentences.zh: 沈林子按劍怒曰：「相公志清六合，今許、洛已定，關右將平，事之濟否，繫於前鋒。

translations.literal: Shen Linzi laid hand on his sword in anger and said: "The Chancellor's aim is to clear the realm; now Xu and Luo are settled and the west of the passes is about to be pacified—whether the affair succeeds or fails hangs on the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Linzi gripped his sword and said in fury: "The Chancellor means to pacify the realm. Xu and Luo are taken; the west of the passes is within reach. Success or failure hangs on us, the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 奈何沮乘勝之氣，棄垂成之功乎！

translations.literal: How can you damp the spirit of victory and abandon a success nearly won!
translations.idiomatic: How can you kill the spirit of victory and throw away a triumph within grasp!

sentences.zh: 且大軍尚遠，賊眾方盛，雖欲求還，豈可得乎！

translations.literal: Moreover the main army is still far off and the enemy host is at its height—even if you wished to return, how could you?
translations.idiomatic: The main army is still far away and the enemy is at full strength—even if we wished to turn back, could we?

sentences.zh: 」下官授命不顧，今日之事，當自為將軍辦之，未知二三君子將何面以見相公之旗鼓邪！

translations.literal: " I received my commission without regard for my life; today's affair I shall see through for the general myself—how will you gentlemen face the Chancellor's banners and drums!
translations.idiomatic: " I took this commission ready to die for it. I will see today's business through for the general myself—what face will you gentlemen show when you stand before the Chancellor's banners and drums?

sentences.zh: 」鎮惡等遣使馳告裕，求遣糧援。

translations.literal: " Zhen'e and the others sent messengers in haste to report to Yu and ask that grain be sent in relief.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhen'e and the others sent urgent messengers to Liu Yu begging for grain.

sentences.zh: 裕呼使者，開舫北戶，指河上魏軍以示之曰：「我語令勿進，今輕佻深入。

translations.literal: Yu summoned the messenger, opened the north door of the boat, pointed to the Wei army on the river to show him, and said: "I told you not to advance; now you have rashly gone deep.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu called the messenger forward, opened the north door of his boat, pointed to the Wei forces on the river, and said: "I told you not to advance. You rushed ahead recklessly.

sentences.zh: 岸上如此，何由得遣軍！

translations.literal: The north bank is like this—how can I send troops!
translations.idiomatic: The north bank looks like this—how am I to send you troops?

sentences.zh: 」鎮惡乃親至弘農，說諭百姓，百姓競送義租，軍食復振。

translations.literal: " Zhen'e then went in person to Hongnong, explained and persuaded the common people, and the people competed to send voluntary grain levies; the army's food was restored.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhen'e went in person to Hongnong, rallied the people, and they vied to send voluntary grain until the army's supplies were restored.

sentences.zh: 魏人以數千騎緣河隨裕軍西行；

translations.literal: The Wei sent several thousand horsemen along the river to follow Yu's army westward;
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent several thousand horsemen along the river to shadow Liu Yu's fleet westward;

sentences.zh: 軍人於南岸牽百丈，風水迅急，有漂渡北岸者，輒為魏人所殺略。

translations.literal: soldiers on the south bank hauled the hundred-zhang cables; wind and current were swift, and those who drifted across to the north bank were killed and plundered by the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: soldiers on the south bank hauled the tow ropes; wind and current ran fierce, and any man who drifted to the north bank was killed or plundered by the Wei.

sentences.zh: 裕遣軍擊之，裁登岸則走，退則復來。

translations.literal: Yu sent troops to strike them; they would flee as soon as they landed on shore and return when the troops withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent troops to drive them off; they fled the moment his men landed and returned as soon as they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，裕遣白直隊主丁晤帥仗士七百人、車百乘，渡北岸，去水百餘步，為卻月陣，兩端抱河，車置七仗士，事畢，使豎一白毦；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Yu sent the leader of the White Guard company Ding Wu to lead seven hundred armored soldiers and one hundred chariots across to the north bank, more than a hundred paces from the water, to form a crescent formation with both ends embracing the river; each chariot carried seven armored soldiers; when all was ready he had a white pennon raised;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Liu Yu sent White Guard company leader Ding Wu with seven hundred armored soldiers and one hundred chariots across to the north bank. More than a hundred paces from the water they formed a crescent with both ends anchored on the river; each chariot held seven armored men. When all was ready a white pennon was raised;

sentences.zh: 魏人不解其意，皆未動。

translations.literal: the Wei did not understand his intent and all held still.
translations.idiomatic: the Wei did not grasp his intent and held their ground.

sentences.zh: 裕先命寧朔將軍朱超石戒嚴，白毦既舉，超石帥二千人馳往赴之，繼大弩百張，一車益二十人，設彭排於轅上。

translations.literal: Yu had earlier ordered the Pacifying-the-North General Zhu Chao Shi to stand ready; once the white pennon was raised, Chao Shi led two thousand men in a gallop to join them, with a hundred large crossbows following; each chariot gained twenty more men, and ramparts were set on the chariot shafts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu had already ordered Pacifying-the-North General Zhu Chao Shi to stand ready. When the white pennon rose, Chao Shi galloped forward with two thousand men and a hundred large crossbows; each chariot took twenty more men and ramparts were mounted on the shafts.

sentences.zh: 魏人見營陣既立，乃進圍之；

translations.literal: When the Wei saw the camp and formation established, they advanced to surround it;
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the camp formed, the Wei advanced to surround it;

sentences.zh: 長孫嵩帥三萬騎助之，四面肉薄攻營，弩不能制。

translations.literal: Changsun Song led thirty thousand horsemen to aid them and attacked the camp on all sides at close quarters; the crossbows could not hold them in check.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Song brought thirty thousand horse to help and pressed the camp on all sides at close range; the crossbows could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 時超石別繼大錘乃槊千餘張，乃斷槊長三四尺，以錘錘之，一槊輒洞貫三四人。

translations.literal: At that time Chao Shi had separately brought more than a thousand great hammers and spears; they cut the spears to three or four chi in length and struck with the hammers—one spear thrust would pierce through three or four men.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Shi had brought more than a thousand heavy hammers and spears. They cut the spears to three or four chi and drove them with the hammers—each thrust ran through three or four men.

sentences.zh: 魏兵不能當，一時奔潰，死者相積；

translations.literal: The Wei troops could not withstand this and at once broke and fled; the dead piled up;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei could not stand against them and broke at once; the dead lay in heaps;

sentences.zh: 臨陳斬阿薄干，魏人退還畔城。

translations.literal: A Bogan was beheaded in the battle line, and the Wei withdrew to Pan city.
translations.idiomatic: A Bogan was killed in the fighting, and the Wei fell back to Pan city.

sentences.zh: 超石帥寧朔將軍胡籓、寧遠將軍劉榮祖追擊，又破之，殺獲千計。

translations.literal: Chao Shi led Ning-shuo General Hu Fan and Ning-yuan General Liu Rongzu in pursuit, again defeated them, and killed and captured in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Shi led Generals Hu Fan and Liu Rongzu in pursuit, routed the enemy again, and killed or captured thousands.

sentences.zh: 魏主嗣聞之，乃恨不用崔浩之言。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler Si heard of it and then regretted not having used Cui Hao's words.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Si of Wei heard this, he bitterly regretted not having heeded Cui Hao's counsel.

sentences.zh: 秦魯公紹遣長史姚洽、寧朔將軍安鸞、護軍姚墨蠡、河東太守唐小方帥眾三千屯河北之九原，阻河為固，欲以絕檀道濟糧援。

translations.literal: Duke of Lu Shao of Qin sent Chief Clerk Yao Qia, Ning-shuo General An Luan, Protector-of-the-Army Yao Mo Li, and Hedong Administrator Tang Xiaofang leading three thousand troops to encamp at Jiuyuan north of the river, blocking the river to make it firm, intending thereby to cut off Tan Daoji's grain and reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Lu Shao of Qin dispatched Chief Clerk Yao Qia, General An Luan, Protector-of-the-Army Yao Mo Li, and Hedong Administrator Tang Xiaofang with three thousand men to hold Jiuyuan north of the Yellow River, using the river as a barrier to sever Tan Daoji's supply lines.

sentences.zh: 沈林子邀擊，破之，斬洽、黑蠡、小方，殺獲殆盡。

translations.literal: Shen Linzi intercepted and attacked, defeated them, beheaded Qia, Hei Li, and Xiaofang, and killed and captured nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Linzi ambushed and routed them, beheading Qia, Mo Li, and Xiaofang; nearly the entire force was killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 林子因啟太尉裕曰：「紹氣蓋關中，今兵屈於外，國危於內。

translations.literal: Linzi thereupon reported to Grand Marshal Yu, saying: "Shao's prestige covers all Guanzhong; now his troops are broken abroad and the state is endangered within.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi then reported to Grand Marshal Liu Yu: "Shao's prestige still dominates Guanzhong, yet his armies are broken abroad and the realm is imperiled within.

sentences.zh: 恐其凶命先盡，不得以膏齊斧耳。

translations.literal: I fear his evil fate will be exhausted first, and he will not get to receive the anointed axe of Qi."
translations.idiomatic: I fear his wicked span will run out first, and he will never live to face your conquering axe."

sentences.zh: 」紹聞洽等敗死，憤恚，發病嘔血，以兵屬東平公贊而卒。

translations.literal: " When Shao heard that Qia and the others were defeated and died, he was furious and resentful; illness broke out and he spat blood; he entrusted the troops to Duke of the East Ping Zan and died.
translations.idiomatic: " When Shao learned that Qia and his fellows had been defeated and killed, rage and grief seized him; he fell ill and vomited blood, entrusted the army to Duke of the East Ping Zan, and died.

sentences.zh: 贊既代紹，眾力猶盛，引兵襲林子，林子復擊破之。

translations.literal: Once Zan had replaced Shao, the collective strength was still formidable; he led troops to attack Linzi, and Linzi again attacked and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: After Zan succeeded Shao, their combined strength remained formidable; he led troops against Linzi, and Linzi defeated him once more.

sentences.zh: 太尉裕至洛陽，行視城塹，嘉毛修之完葺之功，賜衣服玩好，直二千萬。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Yu reached Luoyang, walked and inspected the walls and moats, praised Mao Xiuzhi's accomplishments in completing repairs, and granted robes, curios, and playthings worth twenty million cash.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Liu Yu reached Luoyang, inspected the walls and moats, commended Mao Xiuzhi for restoring them, and rewarded him with robes, ornaments, and valuables worth twenty million cash.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，魏主嗣如高柳。

translations.literal: On ding-si, the Wei ruler Si went to Gaoliu.
translations.idiomatic: On ding-si, Emperor Si of Wei traveled to Gaoliu.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，還平城。

translations.literal: On ren-xu, he returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On ren-xu he went back to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 河西王蒙遜大赦，遣張掖太守沮渠廣宗詐降，以誘涼公歆，歆發兵應之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hexi Meng Xun proclaimed a great amnesty and sent Zhangye Administrator Juqu Guangzong to feign surrender in order to lure Lord of Liang Xin; Xin mobilized troops to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Hexi Meng Xun declared a general amnesty and sent Zhangye Administrator Juqu Guangzong to feign surrender and lure Lord of Liang Xin; Xin raised troops to answer the call.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜將兵三萬伏於蓼泉，歆覺之，引兵還。

translations.literal: Meng Xun led thirty thousand troops in ambush at Liaoshui; Xin detected it and withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xun lay in wait at Liaoshui with thirty thousand men; Xin detected the trap and pulled his army back.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜追之，歆與戰於解支澗，大破之。

translations.literal: Meng Xun pursued him; Xin fought him at Jiezhi Stream and greatly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xun gave chase; Xin met him at Jiezhi Stream and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 斬首七千餘級。

translations.literal: More than seven thousand heads were cut.
translations.idiomatic: More than seven thousand heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜城建康，置戍而還。

translations.literal: Meng Xun walled Jiankang, posted a garrison, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xun fortified Jiankang, left a garrison, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙未，齊郡太守王懿降於魏，上書言：「劉裕在洛，宜發兵絕其歸路，可不戰而克。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on yi-wei, Administrator of Qi Commandery Wang Yi surrendered to Wei and submitted a memorial saying: "Liu Yu is at Luoyang; you should send troops to cut off his line of return, and you can take him without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yi-wei, Administrator of Qi Commandery Wang Yi defected to Wei and wrote: "Liu Yu is at Luoyang. Send troops to sever his retreat, and you can destroy him without a battle.

sentences.zh: 」魏主嗣善之。

translations.literal: " The Wei ruler Si approved of it.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Si of Wei thought well of the proposal.

sentences.zh: 崔浩侍講在前，嗣問之曰：「劉裕伐姚泓，果能克乎？

translations.literal: Cui Hao attended the lecture before the throne; Si asked him, saying: "Liu Yu attacks Yao Hong—can he truly conquer him?
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao was lecturing before the throne when Si asked him: "Liu Yu is campaigning against Yao Hong—can he truly prevail?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「克之。

translations.literal: " He replied: "He can conquer him.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered: "He will prevail.

sentences.zh: 」嗣曰：「何故？

translations.literal: " Si said: "For what reason?
translations.idiomatic: " Si asked: "Why?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「昔姚興好事虛名而少實用，子泓懦而多病，兄弟乖爭。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Formerly Yao Xing loved fine names but had little practical use; his son Hong is timid and frequently ill, and the brothers quarrel among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "Yao Xing once chased empty glory and neglected real strength; his son Hong is weak and sickly, and the brothers are at odds.

sentences.zh: 裕乘其危，兵精將勇，何故不克！

translations.literal: Yu takes advantage of their peril; the troops are elite and the generals brave—why would he not conquer!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu strikes while they are vulnerable, with crack troops and bold commanders—how could he fail!

sentences.zh: 」嗣曰：「裕才何如慕容垂？

translations.literal: " Si said: "How does Yu's talent compare with Murong Chui's?
translations.idiomatic: " Si asked: "How does Liu Yu's talent compare with Murong Chui's?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「勝之。

translations.literal: " He replied: "He surpasses him.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered: "Superior to him.

sentences.zh: 垂藉父兄之資，修復舊業，國人歸之，若夜蟲之就火，少加倚仗，易以立功。

translations.literal: Chui relied on the resources of father and elder brother, restored the old enterprise, and the people of the state came to him like night insects going to fire; with a little reliance he could easily achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: Chui drew on the legacy of father and elder brother, rebuilt the old realm, and his people rallied to him like moths to flame—a little support, and merit came easily.

sentences.zh: 劉裕奮起寒微，不階尺土，討滅桓玄，興復晉室，北禽慕容超，南梟盧循，所向無前，非其才之過人，安能如是乎！

translations.literal: Liu Yu rose up from humble cold beginnings, climbed not one foot of inherited territory, suppressed and destroyed Huan Xuan, revived the Jin house, captured Murong Chao in the north and executed Lu Xun in the south—wherever he turned none stood before him; if not for talent surpassing other men, how could he have done thus!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu rose from utter obscurity without inheriting a foot of land, overthrew Huan Xuan, restored the Jin dynasty, captured Murong Chao in the north and executed Lu Xun in the south, and swept all before him—without genius beyond ordinary men, how could he have done so!

sentences.zh: 」嗣曰：「裕既入關，不能進退，我以精騎直搗彭城、壽春，裕將若之何？

translations.literal: " Si said: "Once Yu has entered the Pass and can neither advance nor retreat, if I send elite cavalry straight against Pengcheng and Shouchun—what will Yu's generals do then?
translations.idiomatic: " Si said: "Once Liu Yu is inside the Pass and cannot advance or withdraw, suppose I send elite cavalry straight at Pengcheng and Shouchun—what can his generals do?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「今西有屈丐，北有柔然，窺伺國隙。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Now in the west there is Helian Bobo, and in the north the Rouran, both watching for gaps in the state.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "Helian Bobo lies to the west and the Rouran to the north, both watching for weakness in our realm.

sentences.zh: 陛下既不可親御六師，雖有精兵，未睹良將。

translations.literal: Your Majesty cannot personally lead the six armies; although there are elite troops, we have not yet seen capable generals.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty cannot lead the armies in person; though we have fine soldiers, we lack proven commanders.

sentences.zh: 長孫嵩長於治國，短於用兵，非劉裕敵也。

translations.literal: Changsun Song excels at governing the state but falls short in using troops; he is not Liu Yu's match.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Song is skilled at statecraft but weak in war—no match for Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 興兵遠攻，未見其利，不如且安靜以待之，裕克秦而歸，必篡其主。

translations.literal: To raise troops for distant attack—I see no profit in it; better for now to keep quiet and wait: when Yu conquers Qin and returns, he is sure to usurp his sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Raising armies for a distant strike offers no clear gain. Better to hold still and wait: when Liu Yu conquers Qin and returns, he will surely usurp his emperor.

sentences.zh: 關中華、戎雜錯，風俗勁悍；

translations.literal: Within the Pass, Chinese and barbarians are mixed and interwoven, and local customs are fierce and hardy;
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong is a jumble of Chinese and barbarians, and its people are fierce by custom;

sentences.zh: 裕欲以荊、揚之化施之函、秦，此無異解衣包火，張羅捕虎；

translations.literal: Yu wishes to apply the culture of Jing and Yang to Hanzhong and Qin—this is no different from taking off one's coat to wrap fire, or spreading nets to catch a tiger;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu would impose the manners of Jing and Yang upon Hanzhong and Qin—no different from wrapping fire in one's cloak or setting nets to catch a tiger;

sentences.zh: 雖留兵守之，人情未洽，趨尚不同，適足為寇敵之資耳。

translations.literal: Even if he leaves troops to guard it, hearts are not united and inclinations differ—this will only supply resources to enemy bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Even if he leaves garrisons behind, hearts will not be won and customs will not align—he will only arm future enemies.

sentences.zh: 願陛下按兵息民以觀其變，秦地終為國家之有。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would hold the army and give the people peace while watching for changes; the Qin lands will in the end become the possession of our state.
translations.idiomatic: Let Your Majesty hold your armies and soothe your people while watching how matters unfold—the Qin lands will become ours in the end.

sentences.zh: 可坐而守也。

translations.literal: We can hold it while sitting still.
translations.idiomatic: We need only sit and wait.

sentences.zh: 」嗣笑曰：「卿料之審矣！

translations.literal: " Si smiled and said: "Your forecast is thorough!
translations.idiomatic: " Si smiled and said: "Your judgment is keen!

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「臣嘗私論近世將相之臣：若王猛之治國，苻堅之管仲也；

translations.literal: " Hao said: "Your servant once privately discussed ministers who were both generals and chancellors in recent times: Wang Meng in governing the state was to Fu Jian what Guan Zhong was;
translations.idiomatic: " Hao said: "I have privately compared the great ministers of recent times: Wang Meng governing the realm was to Fu Jian what Guan Zhong was to Duke Huan;

sentences.zh: 慕容恪之輔幼主，慕容暐之霍光也；

translations.literal: Murong Ke in assisting the young lord was to Murong Wei what Huo Guang was;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke guiding the young sovereign was to Murong Wei what Huo Guang was to Emperor Xuan;

sentences.zh: 劉裕之平禍亂，司馬德宗之曹操也。

translations.literal: Liu Yu in pacifying calamity and disorder was to Sima Dezong what Cao Cao was.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu in quelling chaos was to Sima Dezong what Cao Cao was to Emperor Xian.

sentences.zh: 」嗣曰：「屈丐何如？

translations.literal: " Si said: "What of Helian Bobo?
translations.idiomatic: " Si asked: "What of Helian Bobo?

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：』屈丐國破家覆，孤孑一身，寄食姚氏，受其封殖。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "Helian Bobo's state was destroyed and family overthrown; alone and solitary, a single man, he lived off the Yao clan and received their nurturing and patronage.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao said: "Helian Bobo's realm was shattered and his house ruined; alone and destitute, he lived at the Yao clan's table and accepted their bounty.

sentences.zh: 不思酬恩報義，而乘時繳利，盜有一方，結怨四鄰。

translations.literal: He does not think to repay kindness and return righteousness, but instead seizes the moment to grab profit, robbing one region and making enemies of all four neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: Instead of repaying that kindness, he seized his chance for gain, stole a domain for himself, and made enemies on every side.

sentences.zh: 撅豎小人，雖能縱暴一時，終當為人所吞食耳。

translations.literal: An upstart petty man—though he can indulge violence for a time, in the end he will surely be devoured by others.
translations.idiomatic: A jumped-up scoundrel may rampage for a season, but in the end others will swallow him whole.

sentences.zh: 」嗣大悅，語至夜半，賜浩御縹醪十觚，水精鹽一兩，曰：「朕味卿言，如此鹽、灑，故欲與卿共饗其美。

translations.literal: " Si was greatly pleased; they talked until midnight and he granted Hao ten gallons of imperial green liquor and one liang of crystal salt, saying: "I savor your words as I savor this salt and wine—therefore I wish to share their excellence with you.
translations.idiomatic: " Si was delighted; they talked until midnight, and he gave Hao ten gallons of imperial green wine and one liang of crystal salt, saying: "Your words are to me like this salt and wine—I wish to share their savor with you.

sentences.zh: 」然猶命長孫嵩、叔孫建各簡精兵，伺裕西過，自成皋濟河，南侵彭、沛，若不時過，則引兵隨之。

translations.literal: " Nevertheless he still ordered Changsun Song and Shusun Jian each to select elite troops to watch for Yu's passage west; they were to cross the river at Chenggao, invade south into Peng and Pei—and if he did not pass in season, they were to follow after with their troops.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet he still ordered Changsun Song and Shusun Jian each to pick elite troops and watch for Liu Yu's westward march: they were to cross the river at Chenggao, strike south into Peng and Pei, and if he did not pass in good time, follow in his wake.

sentences.zh: 魏主嗣西巡至雲中，遂濟河，畋於大漠。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler Si toured west as far as Yunzhong, then crossed the river and hunted on the great desert.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Si of Wei toured west to Yunzhong, crossed the river, and hunted on the great steppe.

sentences.zh: 魏置天地四方六部大人，以諸公為之。

translations.literal: Wei established Lords of the Six Departments of Heaven, Earth, and the Four Directions, appointing the princes to these posts.
translations.idiomatic: Wei created six departmental lords for Heaven, Earth, and the four directions, and appointed the princes to fill them.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，太尉裕至陝。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Grand Marshal Yu reached Shan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, Grand Marshal Liu Yu reached Shan.

sentences.zh: 沈田子、傅弘之入武關，秦戍將皆委城走。

translations.literal: Shen Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi entered Wu Pass; the Qin garrison generals all abandoned their cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi entered Wu Pass; every Qin garrison commander abandoned his post and fled.

sentences.zh: 田子等進屯青泥，秦主泓使給事黃門侍郎姚和都屯嶢柳以拒之。

translations.literal: Tianzi and the others advanced to encamp at Qingni; the Qin ruler Hong sent Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate Yao Hedou to encamp at Yaoliu to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi and his men advanced to Qingni; Lord of Qin Yao Hong sent Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate Yao Hedou to hold Yaoliu against them.

sentences.zh: 西秦相國翟勍卒；

translations.literal: Prime Minister of Western Qin Zhai Fu died;
translations.idiomatic: Prime Minister Zhai Fu of Western Qin died;

sentences.zh: 八月，以尚書令曇達為左丞相，右僕射元基為右丞相，御史大夫麴景為尚書令，侍中翟紹為左僕射。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Shangshu Ling Tanda was made Left Chancellor, Right Vice-Director Yuan Ji was made Right Chancellor, Censor-in-Chief Qu Jing was made Shangshu Ling, and Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhai Shao was made Left Vice-Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Tanda was made Left Chancellor, Yuan Ji Right Chancellor, Qu Jing Minister of the Masters of Writing, and Zhai Shao Left Vice-Director.

sentences.zh: 太尉裕至闅鄉，沈田子等將攻嶢柳。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Yu reached Huinxiang; Shen Tianzi and the others were about to attack Yaoliu.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Liu Yu reached Huinxiang, and Shen Tianzi prepared to assault Yaoliu.

sentences.zh: 秦主泓欲自將以御裕軍，恐田子等襲其後，欲先擊滅田子等，然後傾國東出；

translations.literal: The Qin ruler Hong wished to lead the army himself to oppose Yu's forces, but feared Tianzi and the others would strike his rear; he wished first to attack and destroy Tianzi and the others, then commit the whole state to march east;
translations.idiomatic: Lord of Qin Yao Hong meant to lead the army himself against Liu Yu, but feared Tianzi might strike his rear; he resolved first to destroy Tianzi, then throw the whole realm eastward;

sentences.zh: 乃帥步騎數萬，奄至青泥。

translations.literal: He therefore led several tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry and suddenly arrived at Qingni.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore marched with tens of thousands of foot and horse and suddenly appeared at Qingni.

sentences.zh: 田子本為疑兵，所領裁千餘人，聞泓至，欲擊之；

translations.literal: Tianzi had originally been a decoy force, commanding barely more than a thousand men; when he heard Hong had arrived, he wished to attack;
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi's force was only a feint, barely a thousand strong; when he learned Hong was coming, he wanted to attack;

sentences.zh: 傅弘之以眾寡不敵止之，田子曰：「兵貴用奇，不必在眾。

translations.literal: Fu Hongzhi stopped him on grounds that their numbers were too few to match the enemy; Tianzi said: "In war what is prized is the use of the unexpected—it need not lie in numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hongzhi tried to stop him, saying they were too few to fight; Tianzi replied: "War favors the unexpected—it does not depend on numbers.

sentences.zh: 且今眾寡相懸，勢不兩立，若彼結圍既固，則我無所逃矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, now the disparity in numbers is extreme and we cannot coexist; if they establish their encirclement firmly, then we have nowhere to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Our numbers are wildly unequal and we cannot both survive; once they ring us in, we will have nowhere to run.

sentences.zh: 不如乘其始至，營陳未立，先薄之，可以有功。

translations.literal: Better to take advantage of their first arrival, before their camp array is set, and press upon them first—merit can be achieved thus.
translations.idiomatic: Better to strike while they have just arrived and their camp is not yet set—we can still win.

sentences.zh: 」遂帥所領先進，弘之繼之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he led those under his command in advance, Hongzhi following after.
translations.idiomatic: " He led his men forward at once, with Hongzhi close behind.

sentences.zh: 秦兵合圍數重。

translations.literal: Qin troops surrounded them in several ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Qin troops closed around them in ring after ring.

sentences.zh: 田子撫慰士卒曰：「諸君冒險遠來，正求今日之戰，死生一決，封侯之業於此在矣！

translations.literal: Tianzi comforted the soldiers, saying: "You have all come from afar braving danger—precisely to seek today's battle; life and death are decided in one stroke, and the achievement of enfeoffment lies herein!
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi rallied his men: "You came far and risked everything for this day—life and death hang on one clash, and the road to enfeoffment runs through here!

sentences.zh: 」士卒皆踴躍鼓噪，執短兵奮擊，秦兵大敗，斬馘萬餘級，得其乘輿服御物，秦主泓奔還灞上。

translations.literal: " The soldiers all leaped and cheered, grasped short weapons and fought fiercely; the Qin army suffered a great defeat, more than ten thousand heads were cut and counted, and they seized Hong's carriage, insignia, and regalia; the Qin ruler Hong fled back to Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: " The soldiers shouted and surged forward with short blades; the Qin army collapsed. More than ten thousand heads were taken, along with Hong's carriage and regalia, and Lord of Qin Yao Hong fled back to Bashang.

sentences.zh: 初，裕以田子等眾少，遣沈林子將兵自秦嶺往助之，至則秦兵已敗，乃相與追之，關中群縣多潛送款於田子。

translations.literal: Initially, Yu had seen that Tianzi's force was small and dispatched Shen Linzi to lead troops from the Qin Mountains to assist them; when he arrived the Qin army was already defeated, so together they pursued, and many counties of the Guanzhong region secretly sent pledges of allegiance to Tianzi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, seeing Tianzi's force was too small, Liu Yu had sent Shen Linzi south from the Qin Mountains to reinforce him; Linzi arrived after the Qin army was already broken, and together they pursued as counties across Guanzhong secretly pledged themselves to Tianzi.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，太尉裕至潼關，以朱超石為河東太守，使與振武將軍徐猗之會薛帛於河北，共攻蒲阪。

translations.literal: On xin-chou, Grand Marshal Yu reached Tong Pass; he appointed Zhu Chaoshi Administrator of Hedong and had him join Zhenwu General Xu Yizhi at Xuebo north of the river to jointly attack Puban.
translations.idiomatic: On xin-chou, Grand Marshal Liu Yu reached Tong Pass, made Zhu Chaoshi Administrator of Hedong, and ordered him to join General Xu Yizhi at Xuebo north of the river in a joint assault on Puban.

sentences.zh: 秦平原公璞與姚和都共擊之，猗之敗死，超石奔還潼關。

translations.literal: Duke of Pingyuan Pu of Qin and Yao Hedou jointly attacked them; Yizhi was defeated and killed, and Chaoshi fled back to Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Pingyuan Yao Pu and Yao Hedou attacked them together; Yizhi was defeated and killed, and Chaoshi retreated to Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 東平公贊遣司馬國璠引魏兵以躡裕後。

translations.literal: Duke of the East Ping Zan sent Sima Guofan to lead Wei troops to follow on Yu's rear.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of the East Ping Zan sent Sima Guofan to bring Wei troops and shadow Liu Yu's rear.

sentences.zh: 王鎮惡請帥水軍自河入渭以趨長安，裕許之。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen'e requested to lead the water army from the river into the Wei to press toward Chang'an; Yu assented.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e asked to lead the fleet from the Yellow River into the Wei and strike for Chang'an; Liu Yu agreed.

sentences.zh: 秦恢武將軍姚難自香城引兵而西，鎮惡追之；

translations.literal: Qin General Who Restores Military Might Yao Nan led troops west from Xiangcheng, and Zhen'e pursued;
translations.idiomatic: Qin General Who Restores Military Might Yao Nan marched west from Xiangcheng, and Zhen'e gave chase;

sentences.zh: 秦主泓自灞上引兵還屯石橋以為之援，鎮北將軍姚強與難合兵屯涇上以拒鎮惡。

translations.literal: The Qin ruler Hong led troops back from Bashang to encamp at Shiqiao to support him; Zhenbei General Yao Qiang joined Nan's troops to encamp on the Jing River to oppose Zhen'e.
translations.idiomatic: Lord of Qin Yao Hong withdrew from Bashang to Shiqiao to support him; General Who Pacifies the North Yao Qiang joined Nan on the Jing River to block Zhen'e.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡使毛德祖進擊，破之，強死，難奔長安。

translations.literal: Zhen'e sent Mao Dezu forward to attack, defeated them; Qiang died and Nan fled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e sent Mao Dezu forward to attack and routed them; Qiang was killed and Nan fled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 東平公贊退屯鄭城，太尉裕進軍逼之。

translations.literal: Duke of the East Ping Zan withdrew to encamp at Zheng city; Grand Marshal Yu advanced his army and pressed him.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of the East Ping Zan fell back to Zheng city as Grand Marshal Liu Yu advanced and closed in.

sentences.zh: 泓使姚丕守渭橋，胡翼度屯石積，東平公贊屯灞東，泓屯逍遙園。

translations.literal: Hong had Yao Pi hold the Wei Bridge, Hu Yidu encamp at Shiji, Duke of the East Ping Zan encamp east of the Ba, and Hong encamp at Xiaoyao Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Hong posted Yao Pi at the Wei Bridge, Hu Yidu at Shiji, Duke of the East Ping Zan east of the Ba River, and himself at Xiaoyao Garden.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡溯渭而上，乘蒙沖小艦，行船者皆在艦內；

translations.literal: Zhen'e went upstream on the Wei, riding covered-assault boats and small vessels; those rowing the boats all kept inside the vessels;
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e sailed up the Wei in covered assault boats and light craft, with every rower hidden inside;

sentences.zh: 秦人見艦進而無行船者，皆驚以為神。

translations.literal: When the people of Qin saw the boats advancing but no one rowing, they all marvelled and took it for divine.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin people saw the boats glide forward with no oarsmen visible and took it for sorcery.

sentences.zh: 壬戌旦，鎮惡至渭橋，令軍士食畢，皆持仗登岸，後登者斬。

translations.literal: At dawn on ren-xu, Zhen'e reached the Wei Bridge; he ordered the soldiers to finish eating, all to take up weapons and go ashore—whoever boarded last would be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on ren-xu, Zhen'e reached the Wei Bridge, ordered his men to eat their fill, take up arms, and go ashore—any man who came last would be beheaded.

sentences.zh: 眾既登，渭水迅急，艦皆隨流，倏忽不知所在。

translations.literal: Once the masses had gone ashore, the Wei River's current was swift and all the boats drifted away downstream, vanishing in an instant with no one knowing where they were.
translations.idiomatic: Once all were ashore, the Wei ran swift and every boat was swept downstream, vanishing in moments.

sentences.zh: 時泓所將尚數萬人。

translations.literal: At that time the troops Hong commanded still numbered several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Hong still commanded tens of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡諭士卒曰：「吾屬並家在江南，此為長安北門，去家萬里，舟楫、衣糧皆已隨流。

translations.literal: Zhen'e addressed the soldiers, saying: "We all have our homes in the Jiangnan region; this is the north gate of Chang'an, ten thousand li from home, and our boats, clothing, and grain have all gone with the stream.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e told his troops: "Our homes are all in the south; this is Chang'an's north gate, ten thousand li from home, and our boats, clothes, and grain have all been swept away.

sentences.zh: 今進戰而勝，則功名俱顯；

translations.literal: If we fight forward now and win, then fame and merit will both be manifest;
translations.idiomatic: Fight and win, and fame and reward are ours;

sentences.zh: 不勝，則骸骨不返，無它歧矣。

translations.literal: If we do not win, our bones will not return—and there is no other path.
translations.idiomatic: Lose, and our bones will never go home—there is no other way.

sentences.zh: 卿等勉之！

translations.literal: Do your utmost, all of you!
translations.idiomatic: Give me everything you have!

sentences.zh: 」乃身先士卒，眾騰踴爭進，大破姚丕於渭橋。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he took the lead before the soldiers; the masses surged and competed to advance, and greatly defeated Yao Pi at the Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: " He charged at the head of his men; they surged forward and shattered Yao Pi at the Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 泓引兵救之，為丕敗卒所蹂踐，不戰而潰。

translations.literal: Hong led troops to rescue him but was trampled by Pi's routed soldiers and collapsed without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Hong marched to his aid but was overrun by Pi's fleeing troops and broke without a fight.

sentences.zh: 姚諶等皆死，泓單馬還宮。

translations.literal: Yao Chen and the others all died; Hong returned alone on horseback to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chen and others were killed; Hong rode alone back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡入自平朔門，泓與姚裕等數百騎逃奔石橋。

translations.literal: Zhen'e entered through the Pingshuo Gate; Hong fled with Yao Yu and several hundred cavalry toward Shiqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e entered through the Pingshuo Gate as Hong fled with Yao Yu and a few hundred horsemen toward Shiqiao.

sentences.zh: 東平公贊聞泓敗，引兵赴之，眾皆潰去。

translations.literal: When Duke of the East Ping Zan heard Hong was defeated, he led troops to go to his aid, but the masses all dispersed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of the East Ping Zan heard Hong was beaten, he marched to help—but his men scattered and fled.

sentences.zh: 胡翼度降於太尉裕。

translations.literal: Hu Yidu surrendered to Grand Marshal Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yidu surrendered to Grand Marshal Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 泓將出降，其子佛念，年十一，言於泓曰：「晉人將逞其欲，雖降必不免，不如引決。

translations.literal: As Hong was about to go out to surrender, his son Foxinian, eleven years old, said to Hong: "The men of Jin will indulge their desires; even if we surrender we will surely not escape—better to take one's own life.
translations.idiomatic: As Hong prepared to surrender, his eleven-year-old son Foxinian said to him: "The Jin will do as they please; even if we yield, we cannot escape—better to end our own lives.

sentences.zh: 」泓憮然不應，佛念登宮牆自投而死。

translations.literal: " Hong stared blankly and did not answer; Foxinian climbed the palace wall and threw himself down to his death.
translations.idiomatic: " Hong stared in silence; Foxinian climbed the palace wall and cast himself down to his death.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，泓將妻子、群臣詣鎮惡壘門請降，鎮惡以屬吏。

translations.literal: On gui-hai, Hong brought his wife, children, and ministers to the gate of Zhen'e's camp to request surrender; Zhen'e handed him over to the clerks.
translations.idiomatic: On gui-hai, Hong came with his wife, children, and ministers to the gate of Zhen'e's camp to surrender; Zhen'e turned him over to the officials.

sentences.zh: 城中夷、晉六萬餘戶，鎮惡以國恩撫慰，號令嚴肅，百姓安堵。

translations.literal: In the city there were more than sixty thousand households of barbarians and Jin subjects; Zhen'e comforted them with the state's kindness, his orders were strict and solemn, and the people lived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: More than sixty thousand barbarian and Han households remained in the city; Zhen'e reassured them with imperial grace, kept discipline strict, and the people lived undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 九月，太尉裕至長安，鎮惡迎於灞上。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Grand Marshal Yu reached Chang'an; Zhen'e welcomed him at Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Grand Marshal Liu Yu reached Chang'an, and Zhen'e received him at Bashang.

sentences.zh: 裕勞之曰：「成吾霸業者，卿也！

translations.literal: Yu praised him, saying: "You are the one who accomplished my hegemonic enterprise!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu praised him: "You are the man who made my hegemony!

sentences.zh: 」鎮惡再拜謝曰：「明公之威，諸將之力，鎮惡何功之有！

translations.literal: " Zhen'e bowed twice in thanks and said: "It is the awesome authority of the lord and the strength of the generals—what merit has Zhen'e at all!
translations.idiomatic: " Zhen'e bowed twice and replied: "It was your authority and the generals' strength—what merit is mine!

sentences.zh: 」裕笑曰：「卿欲學馮異邪？

translations.literal: " Yu laughed and said: "Do you wish to study Feng Yi?
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Yu laughed: "Are you trying to imitate Feng Yi?

sentences.zh: 」鎮惡性貪，秦府庫盈積，鎮惡盜取不可勝紀；

translations.literal: " Zhen'e was by nature greedy; the Qin treasury was piled high, and Zhen'e stole from it beyond counting;
translations.idiomatic: " Zhen'e was greedy by nature; the Qin treasury overflowed with wealth, and he plundered it beyond reckoning;

sentences.zh: 裕以其功大，不問。

translations.literal: Yu, because his achievement was great, did not inquire into it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, considering his achievement too great, said nothing.

sentences.zh: 或譖諸裕曰：「鎮惡藏姚泓偽輦，將有異志。

translations.literal: Someone slandered Zhen'e to Yu, saying: "Zhen'e is hiding Yao Hong's false imperial carriage and intends disloyal designs.
translations.idiomatic: Someone slandered Wang Zhen'e to Liu Yu, saying, "Zhen'e is hiding Yao Hong's counterfeit imperial carriage and harbors rebellious intent.

sentences.zh: 」裕使人覘之，鎮惡剔取其金銀，棄輦於垣側，裕意乃安。

translations.literal: " Yu sent men to spy on him; Zhen'e stripped out its gold and silver, discarded the carriage beside a wall, and Yu's mind was then at ease.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Yu sent men to investigate. Zhen'e stripped out the gold and silver, threw the carriage aside by a wall, and Liu Yu's suspicions were put to rest.

sentences.zh: 裕收秦彝器、渾儀、土圭、記裡鼓、指南車送詣建康。

translations.literal: Yu collected Qin's ritual vessels, armillary sphere, gnomon, mile-marking drum carriage, and south-pointing chariot and sent them to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu gathered Qin's ritual bronzes, the armillary sphere, the gnomon, the mile-marking drum carriage, and the south-pointing chariot and sent them to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 其餘金玉、繒帛、珍寶，皆以頒賜將士。

translations.literal: The rest of the gold, jade, silks, and treasures he all distributed in reward to officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining gold, jade, silks, and treasures he distributed among his officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 秦平原公璞、并州刺史尹昭以蒲阪降，東平公贊帥宗族百餘人詣裕降，裕皆殺之。

translations.literal: Qin's Duke of Pingyuan Pu and Bingzhou Inspector Yin Zhao surrendered at Puban; Duke of the East Ping Zan led more than a hundred clansmen to Yu to surrender, and Yu had them all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's Duke of Pingyuan, Yao Pu, and Bingzhou Inspector Yin Zhao surrendered at Puban. Duke of the East Ping, Yao Zan, led more than a hundred kinsmen to surrender to Liu Yu, and Liu Yu had them all executed.

sentences.zh: 送姚泓至建康，斬於市。

translations.literal: He sent Yao Hong to Jiankang and executed him in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong was sent to Jiankang and beheaded in the public square.

sentences.zh: 裕以薛辯為平陽太守，使鎮捍北道。

translations.literal: Yu appointed Xue Bian Administrator of Pingyang and had him garrison and defend the northern route.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu made Xue Bian Administrator of Pingyang and stationed him to hold the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 裕議遷都洛陽，諮議參軍王仲德曰：「非常之事，固非常人所及，必致駭動。

translations.literal: Yu discussed moving the capital to Luoyang; Advisory Attendant Wang Zhongde said: "An extraordinary affair is naturally beyond what ordinary men can grasp and is sure to cause alarm and upheaval.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu proposed moving the capital to Luoyang. Advisory Attendant Wang Zhongde said, "An extraordinary measure is naturally beyond ordinary men and is bound to cause shock and unrest.

sentences.zh: 今暴師日久，士卒思歸，遷都之計，未可議也。

translations.literal: Now the army has been in the field a long time and the soldiers long for home; the plan to move the capital cannot yet be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: The army has been in the field too long, and the men are homesick. The question of moving the capital cannot be broached yet.

sentences.zh: 裕乃止。

translations.literal: Yu then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 羌眾十餘萬口西奔隴上，沈林子追擊至槐裡，俘虜萬計。

translations.literal: More than a hundred thousand Qiang people fled west to Longshang; Shen Linzi pursued and struck them as far as Huaili, capturing prisoners by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred thousand Qiang fled west into Longshang. Shen Linzi pursued them to Huaili and took captives numbering in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 河西王蒙遜聞太尉裕滅秦，怒甚。

translations.literal: Lord of Hexi Mengsun heard that Grand Marshal Yu had destroyed Qin and was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: When Lord of Hexi Ju Mengsun learned that Grand Marshal Liu Yu had destroyed Qin, he was furious.

sentences.zh: 門下校郎劉祥入言事，蒙遜曰：「汝聞劉裕入關，敢謂群臣曰：「姚泓非裕敵也。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Liu Xiang entered to report affairs; Mengsun said: "You heard Liu Yu enter the Pass, yet dared to tell the ministers: 'Yao Hong is no match for Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Liu Xiang came in on business. Mengsun said, "When Liu Yu entered the Pass, you dared tell the court, 'Yao Hong is no match for Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 且其兄弟內叛，安能拒人！

translations.literal: Moreover, his brothers rebelled within—how could he resist others!
translations.idiomatic: His own brothers turned against him from within—how could he hold anyone off!

sentences.zh: 裕取關中必矣。

translations.literal: Yu will surely take Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu is certain to take Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 然裕不能久留，必將南歸，留子弟及諸將守之，吾取之如拾芥耳。

translations.literal: Yet Yu cannot stay long; he is sure to return south, leaving sons, younger brothers, and generals to hold it—I shall take it as easily as picking up a mustard seed.
translations.idiomatic: But Liu Yu cannot stay long. He is sure to return south and leave sons, brothers, and generals to hold the region. I shall take it as easily as picking up a mustard seed.

sentences.zh: 」乃秣馬礪兵，訓養士卒，進據安定，秦嶺北郡縣鎮戍皆降之。

translations.literal: " He then fed the horses and sharpened weapons, trained and nurtured the soldiers, advanced and seized Anding, and the commanderies, counties, and garrison posts north of the Qinling all surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: " He then fed his horses, honed his arms, drilled his troops, advanced to occupy Anding, and the commanderies, counties, and garrisons north of the Qinling all submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 裕遺使遺勃勃書，約為兄弟；

translations.literal: Yu sent an envoy with a letter to Bobo, proposing brotherhood;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent an envoy with a letter to Helian Bobo, proposing a pact of brotherhood;

sentences.zh: 勃勃使中書侍郎皇甫徽為報書而陰育之，對裕使者，口授舍人使書之。

translations.literal: Bobo had Palace Secretariat Attendant Huangfu Hui draft the reply while secretly cultivating him; facing Yu's envoy, he orally dictated to a secretary-attendant to write it.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo had Palace Secretariat Attendant Huangfu Hui compose the reply while secretly grooming him for the task. Facing Liu Yu's envoy, he dictated the text to a secretary-attendant to write down.

sentences.zh: 裕讀其文，歎曰：「吾不如也！

translations.literal: Yu read the text and sighed: "I am not his equal!
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu read the letter, he sighed and said, "I am not his equal!

sentences.zh: 廣州刺史謝欣卒，東海人徐道期聚眾攻陷州城，進攻始興，始興相彭城劉廉之討誅之。

translations.literal: Guangzhou Inspector Xie Xin died; Xu Daoqi of Donghai gathered a crowd, stormed and seized the provincial city, advanced to attack Shixing, and Shixing Chancellor Liu Lianzhi of Pengcheng attacked and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou Inspector Xie Xin died. Xu Daoqi of Donghai raised a mob, stormed the provincial capital, and marched on Shixing. Shixing Chancellor Liu Lianzhi of Pengcheng defeated and killed him.

sentences.zh: 詔以謙之為廣州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Qianzhi Guangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Qianzhi Inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，司馬休之、司馬文思、司馬國璠、司馬道賜、魯軌、韓延之、刁雍、王慧龍及桓溫之孫道度、道子、族人桓謐、桓璲、陳郡袁式等皆詣魏長孫嵩降。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Sima Xiuzhi, Sima Wensi, Sima Guofan, Sima Daosi, Lu Gui, Han Yanzhi, Diao Yong, Wang Huilong, and Huan Wen's grandsons Daodu and Daozi, clansmen Huan Mi and Huan Ji, Chen Commandery's Yuan Shi, and others all went to Wei and surrendered to Changsun Song.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Sima Xiuzhi, Sima Wensi, Sima Guofan, Sima Daosi, Lu Gui, Han Yanzhi, Diao Yong, Wang Huilong, Huan Wen's grandsons Daodu and Daozi, kinsmen Huan Mi and Huan Ji, Yuan Shi of Chen Commandery, and others all went over to Wei and surrendered to Changsun Song.

sentences.zh: 秦匈奴鎮將姚成都及弟和都舉鎮降魏。

translations.literal: Qin's Xiongnu Garrison General Yao Chengdu and his younger brother Hedou raised the garrison and surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's Xiongnu Garrison General Yao Chengdu and his younger brother Hedou surrendered the garrison to Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏主嗣詔民間得姚氏子弟送平城者賞之。

translations.literal: Wei ruler Si issued an edict that whoever among the people captured Yao clansmen and sent them to Pingcheng would be rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Si of Wei decreed that anyone who captured members of the Yao clan and sent them to Pingcheng would be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己酉，嗣召長孫嵩等還。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiyou, Si summoned Changsun Song and the others back.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiyou, Emperor Si recalled Changsun Song and his forces.

sentences.zh: 司馬休之尋卒於魏。

translations.literal: Sima Xiuzhi soon died in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi soon died in Wei territory.

sentences.zh: 魏賜國璠爵淮南公，道賜爵池陽子，魯軌爵襄陽公。

translations.literal: Wei enfeoffed Guofan as Duke of Huainan, Daosi as Marquis of Chiyang, and Lu Gui as Duke of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei enfeoffed Guofan as Duke of Huainan, Daosi as Marquis of Chiyang, and Lu Gui as Duke of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 刁雍表求南鄙自效，嗣以雍為建義將軍。

translations.literal: Diao Yong memorialized asking to serve on the southern frontier; Si made Yong General Who Establishes Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Yong submitted a memorial offering to serve on the southern frontier. Emperor Si appointed him General Who Establishes Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 雍聚眾於河、濟之間，擾動徐、兗；

translations.literal: Yong gathered followers between the Yellow and Ji Rivers, stirring up Xu and Yan;
translations.idiomatic: Diao Yong gathered forces between the Yellow and Ji Rivers and harassed Xu and Yan;

sentences.zh: 太尉裕遣兵討之，不克，雍進屯固山，眾至二萬。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Yu sent troops to attack him but could not overcome him; Yong advanced and encamped at Gushan, and his followers reached twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Liu Yu sent troops against him but failed to defeat him. Diao Yong advanced to Gushan, where his force grew to twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 詔進宋公爵為王，增封十郡；

translations.literal: An edict advanced the Duke of Song to king and added ten commanderies to his fief;
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted the Duke of Song to king and added ten commanderies to his domain;

sentences.zh: 辭不受。

translations.literal: He declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the honor.

sentences.zh: 西秦王熾磐遣左丞相曇達等擊秦故將姚艾，艾遣使稱籓，熾磐以艾為征東大將軍、秦州牧。

translations.literal: King of Western Qin Chipan sent Left Chancellor Tanda and others to attack Qin's former general Yao Ai; Ai sent envoys declaring himself a vassal, and Chipan made Ai Grand General Who Campaigns East and Governor of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: King Chipan of Western Qin sent Left Chancellor Tanda and others against Qin's former general Yao Ai. Ai sent envoys to declare vassalage, and Chipan appointed him Grand General Who Campaigns East and Governor of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 征王松壽為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He summoned Wang Songshou to be Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Wang Songshou to serve as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 十一月，魏叔孫建等討西山丁零翟蜀洛支等，平之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Wei's Shusun Jian and others attacked the Western Mountain Dingling Zhai Shuluozhi and others and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Shusun Jian of Wei and others suppressed the Western Mountain Dingling under Zhai Shuluozhi and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 辛未，劉穆之卒。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Liu Muzhi died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Liu Muzhi died.

sentences.zh: 太尉裕聞之，驚慟哀惋者累日。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Yu heard of it and was shocked, grieved, and sorrowful for many days.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Marshal Liu Yu heard the news, he was stunned and mourned for days.

sentences.zh: 始，裕欲留長安經略西北，而諸將佐皆久役思歸，多不欲留。

translations.literal: At first Yu wished to remain at Chang'an to plan and manage the northwest, but the generals and aides had long been on campaign and longed to return; most did not wish to stay.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu had originally intended to remain at Chang'an and consolidate the northwest, but his generals and staff, weary from long service, were eager to go home, and most did not want to stay.

sentences.zh: 會穆之卒，裕以根本無托，遂決意東還。

translations.literal: When Muzhi died, Yu, because he had no support at his base, then resolved to return east.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzhi died, Liu Yu, left without support at home, resolved to return east.

sentences.zh: 穆之之卒也，朝廷恇懼，欲發詔，以太尉左司馬徐羨之代之，中軍咨議參軍張邵曰：「今誠急病，任終在徐；

translations.literal: When Muzhi died, the court was fearful and alarmed and wished to issue an edict appointing Grand Marshal Left Assistant Xu Xianzhi to replace him; Central Army Advisory Attendant Zhang Shao said: "The present crisis is indeed urgent, and the appointment should ultimately fall to Xu;
translations.idiomatic: When Muzhi died, the court was alarmed and wanted to issue an edict appointing Grand Marshal Left Assistant Xu Xianzhi to replace him. Central Army Advisory Attendant Zhang Shao said, "The crisis is urgent, and Xu is the right man for the post;

sentences.zh: 然世子無專命，宜須諮之。

translations.literal: yet the heir has no authority to decide alone, and one should consult him.
translations.idiomatic: but the heir lacks independent authority. We should consult him first.

sentences.zh: 」裕欲以王弘代穆之，從事中郎謝晦曰：「休元輕易，不若羨之。

translations.literal: " Yu wished to have Wang Hong replace Muzhi; Attendant Gentleman Xie Hui said: "Xiuyuan is frivolous and is not the equal of Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Yu wanted Wang Hong to replace Muzhi. Attendant Gentleman Xie Hui said, "Xiuyuan is too light-minded—not as reliable as Xianzhi.

sentences.zh: 」乃羨之為吏部尚書、建威將軍、丹陽尹，代管留任。

translations.literal: " Xianzhi was then made Director of the Masters of Writing for Personnel, General Who Establishes Might, and Governor of Danyang, managing affairs in Yu's absence.
translations.idiomatic: " So Xianzhi was made Director of the Masters of Writing for Personnel, General Who Establishes Might, and Governor of Danyang, to manage affairs while Liu Yu was away.

sentences.zh: 於是朝廷大事常決於穆之者，並悉北咨。

translations.literal: Thereupon all major court affairs that had regularly been decided by Muzhi were all referred north for consultation.
