translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, all major court decisions that had once rested with Muzhi were referred north to Liu Yu for approval.

sentences.zh: 裕以次子桂陽公義真為都督雍、梁、秦王州諸軍事、安西將軍、領雍、東秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: Yu made his second son, Prince of Guiyang Yizhen, Area Commander over all military affairs of Yong, Liang, and the three Qin provinces, Pacifying-the-West General, and concurrent Inspector of Yong and Eastern Qin provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu appointed his second son, Prince of Guiyang Yizhen, Area Commander over Yong, Liang, and the three Qin provinces, Pacifying-the-West General, and concurrent Inspector of Yong and Eastern Qin.

sentences.zh: 義真時年十二。

translations.literal: Yizhen was then twelve years old.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen was twelve years old at the time.

sentences.zh: 以太尉咨議參軍京兆王修為長史，王鎮惡為司馬、領馮翊太守，沈田子、毛德祖皆為中兵參軍，仍以田子領始平太守，德祖領秦州刺史、天水太守，傅弘之為雍州治中從事史。

translations.literal: He made Grand Marshal Advisory Attendant Wang Xiu of Jingzhao Chief Clerk; Wang Zhen'e Vice Commander and concurrent Administrator of Fufeng; Shen Tianzi and Mao Dezu both Central Army Attendants; Tianzi also held Administrator of Shiping; Dezu held Inspector of Qin Province and Administrator of Tianshui; and Fu Hongzhi was Chief Aide of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Grand Marshal Advisory Attendant Wang Xiu of Jingzhao as Chief Clerk; Wang Zhen'e as Vice Commander and concurrent Administrator of Fufeng; Shen Tianzi and Mao Dezu as Central Army Attendants; Tianzi also as Administrator of Shiping; Dezu as Inspector of Qin Province and Administrator of Tianshui; and Fu Hongzhi as Chief Aide of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 先是，隴上流戶寓關中者，望因兵威得復本土；

translations.literal: Earlier, upstream households from Long who had settled in Guanzhong hoped that through military might they could return to their native lands;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, migrant households from upstream Long who had settled in Guanzhong had hoped that Liu Yu's military power would let them return home;

sentences.zh: 及置東秦州，知裕無復西略之意，皆歎息失望。

translations.literal: when Eastern Qin Province was established, they knew Yu had no further intention of campaigning west and all sighed in disappointment.
translations.idiomatic: when Eastern Qin Province was established, they realized Liu Yu had no further ambition in the west, and all sighed in disappointment.

sentences.zh: 關中人素重王猛，裕之克長安，王鎮惡功為多，由是南人皆忌之。

translations.literal: The people of Guanzhong had always esteemed Wang Meng; in Yu's capture of Chang'an, Wang Zhen'e's achievement was greatest, and for this reason the southerners all envied him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Guanzhong had long revered Wang Meng. In Liu Yu's capture of Chang'an, Wang Zhen'e's service had been greatest, and for that reason the southerners all resented him.

sentences.zh: 沈田子自以嶢柳之捷，與鎮惡爭功不平。

translations.literal: Shen Tianzi, considering himself victor at Yaoliu, was resentful at competing for merit with Zhen'e.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tianzi, crediting himself with the victory at Yaoliu, resented sharing glory with Zhen'e.

sentences.zh: 裕將還，田子及傅弘之屢言於裕曰：「鎮惡家在關中，不可保信。

translations.literal: When Yu was about to return, Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi repeatedly said to Yu: "Zhen'e's family is in Guanzhong and cannot be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: As Liu Yu prepared to return east, Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi repeatedly told him, "Zhen'e's family is in Guanzhong. He cannot be trusted.

sentences.zh: 」裕曰：「今留卿文武將士精兵萬人，彼若欲為不善，正足自滅耳。

translations.literal: " Yu said: "Now I leave you civil and military officers and elite troops numbering ten thousand; if he wishes to do wrong, that is just enough for him to destroy himself.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Yu replied, "I am leaving you civil and military officers with ten thousand picked troops. If he tries anything, he will only destroy himself.

sentences.zh: 勿復多言。

translations.literal: Do not speak of this again.
translations.idiomatic: Say no more of it.

sentences.zh: 」裕私謂田子曰：「鐘會不得遂其亂者，以有衛瓘故也。

translations.literal: " Yu privately told Tianzi: "Zhong Hui could not carry out his rebellion because Wei Guan was there.
translations.idiomatic: " Privately Liu Yu told Tianzi, "Zhong Hui failed in his rebellion because Wei Guan was there to stop him.

sentences.zh: 語曰：『猛獸不如群狐』，卿等十餘人，何懼王鎮惡！

translations.literal: The saying goes, 'A fierce beast is no match for a pack of foxes'—you are more than ten; what is there to fear from Wang Zhen'e!
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, 'A fierce beast is no match for a pack of foxes.' There are more than ten of you—what need is there to fear Wang Zhen'e!

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：古人有言：「疑則勿任，任則勿疑。

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: The ancients had a saying: "If you doubt, do not appoint; if you appoint, do not doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Master Guang remarks: The ancients said, "When in doubt, do not appoint; once appointed, do not doubt.

sentences.zh: 」裕既委鎮惡以關中，而復與田子有後言，是斗之使為亂也。

translations.literal: " Yu had already entrusted Guanzhong to Zhen'e, yet again had private words with Tianzi—this was goading him toward rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Yu had entrusted Guanzhong to Zhen'e, yet whispered otherwise to Tianzi—this was practically inviting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 惜乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: What a pity!

sentences.zh: 百年之寇，千里之士，得之艱難，失之造次，使豐、鄗之都復輸寇手。

translations.literal: A century-old foe, a thousand-li territory—won with difficulty, lost in haste, causing the capitals of Feng and Hao to fall again into the enemy's hands.
translations.idiomatic: A land a century in enemy hands, a thousand li of territory—won only after great hardship, lost in reckless haste, so that the ancient capitals of Feng and Hao passed once more into invader hands.

sentences.zh: 荀子曰：「兼併易能也，堅凝之難。

translations.literal: Xunzi said: "Conquest is easy to accomplish; consolidation is hard.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzi said, "Conquest is easy; holding and consolidating what is won is hard.

sentences.zh: 」信哉！

translations.literal: " How true!
translations.idiomatic: " How true that is!

sentences.zh: 三秦父老聞裕將還，詣門流涕訴曰：「殘民不沾王化，於今百年，始睹衣冠，人人相賀。

translations.literal: The elders of the Three Qins, hearing Yu was about to return, came to his gate weeping and pleaded: "We broken people have not received the king's transforming influence for a hundred years now; we have only just seen official robes and caps, and every man congratulates his neighbor.
translations.idiomatic: The elders of the Three Qins, hearing that Liu Yu was about to leave, came to his gate in tears and pleaded, "We have lived as a broken people outside the king's civilizing rule for a century. We have only just seen officials in court dress again, and every man rejoices with his neighbor.

sentences.zh: 長安十陵是公家墳墓，咸陽宮殿是公家室宅，捨此欲何之乎！

translations.literal: The ten imperial tombs at Chang'an are your family's graves; the palaces at Xianyang are your family's dwellings—leaving these, where do you mean to go!
translations.idiomatic: The ten imperial tombs at Chang'an are your family's graves, and the palaces at Xianyang are your family's home. Where can you go but here!

sentences.zh: 」裕為之愍然，慰諭之曰：「受命朝廷，不得擅留。

translations.literal: " Yu was moved with compassion for them and consoled them, saying: "I have received orders from the court and cannot remain on my own authority.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Yu was deeply moved and consoled them: "I serve at the court's command and cannot stay without authorization.

sentences.zh: 誠多諸君懷本之志，今以次息與文武賢才共鎮此境，勉與之居。

translations.literal: I truly understand your wish to return to your roots; now my younger son together with civil and military worthies will jointly garrison this region—do your best to dwell with them.
translations.idiomatic: I know how deeply you long for home. I leave my younger son here with able civil and military men to hold this land. Do your best to stay and live with them.

sentences.zh: 」十二月，庚子，裕發長安，自洛入河，開汴渠以歸。

translations.literal: " In the twelfth month, on gengzi, Yu set out from Chang'an, entered the river from Luoyang, opened the Bian Canal, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twelfth month, on gengzi, Liu Yu departed Chang'an, entered the Yellow River from Luoyang, opened the Bian Canal, and headed home.

sentences.zh: 氐豪徐駭奴、齊元子等擁部落三萬在雍，遣使請降於魏。

translations.literal: Di chieftains Xu Hainu, Qi Yuanzi, and others, holding a tribe of thirty thousand at Yong, sent envoys requesting surrender to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Di chieftains Xu Hainu, Qi Yuanzi, and others, leading a tribe of thirty thousand at Yong, sent envoys to surrender to Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏主嗣遣將軍王洛生、河內太守楊聲等西行以應之。

translations.literal: Wei ruler Si sent General Wang Luosheng, Henei Administrator Yang Sheng, and others west to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Si of Wei sent General Wang Luosheng, Henei Administrator Yang Sheng, and others west to meet them.

sentences.zh: 閏月，壬申，魏主嗣如大寧長川。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on renshen, Wei ruler Si went to Daning Changchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on renshen, Emperor Si of Wei traveled to Daning Changchuan.

sentences.zh: 秦、雍人千餘家推襄邑令上谷寇贊為主，以降於魏，魏主嗣拜贊魏郡太守。

translations.literal: More than a thousand households of Qin and Yong people made Xiangyi Magistrate Kou Zan of Shanggu their leader and surrendered to Wei; Wei ruler Si appointed Zan Administrator of Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand Qin and Yong households made Xiangyi Magistrate Kou Zan of Shanggu their leader and surrendered to Wei. Emperor Si appointed Zan Administrator of Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 久之，秦、雍人流入魏之河南、滎陽、河內者，戶以萬數。

translations.literal: After some time, Qin and Yong people who flowed into Wei's Henan, Xingyang, and Henei numbered households in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In time, Qin and Yong refugees who fled into Wei's Henan, Xingyang, and Henei numbered in the tens of thousands of households.

sentences.zh: 嗣乃置南雍州，以贊為刺史，封河南公，治洛陽，立雍州郡縣以撫之。

translations.literal: Si then established Southern Yong Province, made Zan its Inspector, enfeoffed him as Duke of Henan, administered from Luoyang, and set up Yong Province commanderies and counties to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Si then established Southern Yong Province, made Zan its Inspector, enfeoffed him Duke of Henan, and governed from Luoyang, establishing Yong commanderies and counties to settle the refugees.

sentences.zh: 贊善於招懷，流民歸之者，三倍其初。

translations.literal: Zan was skilled at winning people over; refugees who returned to him tripled the original number.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was skilled at winning people over, and the refugees who came to him eventually tripled the original number.

sentences.zh: 夏王勃勃聞太尉裕東還，大喜，問於王買德曰：「騰欲取關中，卿試言其方略。

translations.literal: King of Xia Bobo heard Grand Marshal Yu was returning east and was greatly pleased; he asked Wang Maide: "Teng wishes to take Guanzhong—try to describe the strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When King Bobo of Xia heard that Grand Marshal Liu Yu was returning east, he was delighted. He asked Wang Maide, "I mean to take Guanzhong. Tell me your strategy.

sentences.zh: 」買德曰：「關中形勝之地，而裕以幼子守之。

translations.literal: " Maide said: "Guanzhong is a strategically superior land, yet Yu leaves a young son to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: " Maide said, "Guanzhong is a land of natural strength, yet Liu Yu has left a young son to hold it.

sentences.zh: 狼狽而歸，正欲急成篡事耳，不暇復以中原為意。

translations.literal: He returns in disarray, precisely because he wishes urgently to complete his usurpation and has no leisure to think again of the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: He is hurrying home in disarray because he wants to seize the throne at once and will have no time to think of the Central Plains again.

sentences.zh: 此天以關中賜我，不可失也。

translations.literal: Heaven is giving Guanzhong to us—this opportunity must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is handing Guanzhong to us. We must not let the chance slip.

sentences.zh: 青泥、上洛，南北之險要，宜先遣遊軍斷之；

translations.literal: Qingni and Shangluo are strategic passes north and south; one should first send mobile troops to cut them off;
translations.idiomatic: Qingni and Shangluo are the vital passes north and south. Send mobile troops first to seize them;

sentences.zh: 東塞潼關，絕其水陸之路；

translations.literal: block Tong Pass to the east and cut off its routes by water and land;
translations.idiomatic: block Tong Pass to the east and cut off their routes by land and water;

sentences.zh: 然後傳檄三輔，施以威德，則義真在網罟之中，不足取也。

translations.literal: then issue proclamations throughout the Three Adjuncts and apply both might and virtue—then Yizhen will be in a net and snare and is not worth the taking.
translations.idiomatic: then issue proclamations across the Three Adjuncts and apply both force and kindness. Yizhen will be caught in a net and will be easy to take.

sentences.zh: 」勃勃乃以其子撫軍大將軍瑰都督前鋒諸軍事，帥騎二萬向長安。

translations.literal: " Bobo then made his son, Pacification-Army Grand General Gui, Commander of Vanguard Military Affairs, leading twenty thousand cavalry toward Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: " Bobo then made his son, Pacification-Army Grand General Helian Gui, Commander of the Vanguard, and sent him with twenty thousand cavalry toward Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 前將軍昌屯潼關，以買德為撫軍右長史，屯青泥，勃勃將大軍為後繼。

translations.literal: Forward General Chang encamped at Tong Pass; Maide was made Right Chief Clerk of the Pacification Army and encamped at Qingni; Bobo led the main army as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Forward General Chang held Tong Pass. Maide was made Right Chief Clerk of the Pacification Army and encamped at Qingni. Bobo followed with the main army.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏都坐大官章安侯封懿卒。

translations.literal: This year, Wei's Director of the Imperial Kitchen, Marquis of Zhang'an Feng Yi, died.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Wei's Director of the Imperial Kitchen, Marquis of Zhang'an Feng Yi, died.

sentences.zh: 安皇帝癸義熙十四年（

translations.literal: Emperor An, gui, fourteenth year of Yixi (
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Yixi during the reign of Emperor An (

sentences.zh: 戊午，公元四一八年）

translations.literal: wuwu, the year 418 CE)
translations.idiomatic: wuwu, the year 418 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁酉朔，魏主嗣至平城，命護高車中郎將薛繁帥高車、丁零北略，至弱水而還。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on dingyou, the first day of the month, Wei ruler Si reached Pingcheng and ordered Guardian of the Gaoche Central Palace Gentleman Xue Fan to lead Gaoche and Dingling north on campaign, reaching the Ruoshui and returning.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on dingyou, the new moon, Emperor Si of Wei reached Pingcheng and ordered Guardian of the Gaoche Central Palace Gentleman Xue Fan to lead Gaoche and Dingling forces north. They reached the Ruoshui and returned.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinsi, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 夏赫連瑰至渭陽，關中民降之者屬路。

translations.literal: Xia's Helian Gui reached Weiyang; Guanzhong people surrendering to him lined the road.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Gui of Xia reached Weiyang, and Guanzhong people surrendering to him filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍沈田子將兵拒之，畏其眾盛，退屯劉回堡，遣使還報王鎮惡。

translations.literal: Flying-Dragon General Shen Tianzi led troops to resist him; fearing their great numbers, he withdrew and encamped at Liuhui Fortress and sent a messenger back to report to Wang Zhen'e.
translations.idiomatic: Flying-Dragon General Shen Tianzi marched to oppose him. Fearing the enemy's numbers, he fell back to Liuhui Fortress and sent a messenger to report to Wang Zhen'e.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡謂王修曰：「公以十歲兒付吾屬，當共思竭力；

translations.literal: Zhen'e said to Wang Xiu: "The lord entrusted a ten-year-old boy to our care—we should together think how to exert ourselves fully;
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e told Wang Xiu, "The lord entrusted a ten-year-old boy to our care. We should devote ourselves wholeheartedly together;

sentences.zh: 而擁兵不進，虜何由得平！

translations.literal: yet you hold troops and do not advance—how can the enemy be pacified!
translations.idiomatic: yet you hold your troops back and refuse to advance. How can the enemy ever be defeated!

sentences.zh: 」使者還，以告田子。

translations.literal: " The messenger returned and told Tianzi.
translations.idiomatic: " When the messenger returned and told Tianzi,

sentences.zh: 田子與鎮惡素有相圖之志，由是益忿懼。

translations.literal: Tianzi and Zhen'e had long harbored mutual designs against each other, and for this reason he became all the more resentful and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi and Zhen'e had long plotted against each other, and he grew all the more angry and afraid.

sentences.zh: 未幾，鎮惡與田子俱出北地以拒夏兵，軍中訛言：「鎮惡欲盡殺南人，以數十人送義真南還。

translations.literal: Before long, Zhen'e and Tianzi both went out to Beidi to resist Xia troops; a false rumor spread in the army: "Zhen'e wishes to kill all the southerners, send a few dozen men to escort Yizhen south,
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Zhen'e and Tianzi both marched to Beidi to resist the Xia army. A false rumor spread through the camp: "Zhen'e plans to kill all the southerners, send a few dozen men to escort Yizhen south,

sentences.zh: 因據關中反。

translations.literal: and then seize Guanzhong and rebel.
translations.idiomatic: and then seize Guanzhong and rebel.

sentences.zh: 」辛亥，田子請鎮惡至傅弘之營計事。

translations.literal: " On xinhai, Tianzi invited Zhen'e to Fu Hongzhi's camp to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " On xinhai, Tianzi invited Zhen'e to Fu Hongzhi's camp to discuss plans.

sentences.zh: 田子求屏人語，使其宗人沈敬仁斬之幕下，矯稱受太尉令誅之。

translations.literal: Tianzi asked that others be dismissed and speak in private; he had his clansman Shen Jingren behead Zhen'e beneath the tent, and falsely claimed he had received the Grand Marshal's order to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi sent everyone else away, then had his kinsman Shen Jingren cut Wang Zhen'e down under the tent awning and falsely announced that he had acted on the Grand Marshal's orders.

sentences.zh: 弘之奔告劉義真，義真與王修被甲登橫門以察其變。

translations.literal: Hongzhi ran to report to Liu Yizhen; Yizhen and Wang Xiu donned armor and climbed the Heng Gate to observe the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi raced to warn Liu Yizhen. Yizhen and Wang Xiu armed themselves and mounted the Heng Gate to watch for trouble.

sentences.zh: 俄而田子帥數十人來至，言鎮惡反。

translations.literal: Before long, Tianzi arrived leading several dozen men and declared that Zhen'e had rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Tianzi appeared at the head of several dozen men, claiming that Zhen'e had risen in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 修執田子，數以專戮，斬之；

translations.literal: Xiu seized Tianzi, rebuked him for unauthorized execution, and beheaded him;
translations.idiomatic: Xiu seized Tianzi, upbraided him for killing a man on his own authority, and had him beheaded;

sentences.zh: 以冠軍將軍毛修之代鎮惡為安西司馬。

translations.literal: He appointed Champion General Mao Xiuzhi to replace Zhen'e as Pacifying-the-West Major.
translations.idiomatic: he then appointed Champion General Mao Xiuzhi to succeed Zhen'e as Pacifying-the-West Major.

sentences.zh: 傅弘之大破赫連瑰於池陽，又破之於寡婦渡，斬獲甚眾，夏兵乃退。

translations.literal: Fu Hongzhi routed Helian Gui at Chiyang, defeated him again at Widow's Ford, killed and captured a great many, and the Xia army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hongzhi shattered Helian Gui at Chiyang, routed him again at Widow's Ford, and took a vast toll in killed and captured before the Xia army finally withdrew.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，太尉裕至彭城，解嚴，琅邪王德文先歸建康。

translations.literal: On renxu, Grand Marshal Yu reached Pengcheng, lifted martial law, and Prince of Langye Dewen returned to Jiankang first.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu the Grand Marshal Yu reached Pengcheng and lifted the wartime restrictions. Prince of Langye Dewen went on ahead to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 裕聞王鎮惡死，表言「沈田子忽發狂易，奄害忠勳」，追贈鎮惡左將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: When Yu learned of Wang Zhen'e's death, he memorialized that "Shen Tianzi suddenly went mad and violently killed a loyal meritorious officer," and posthumously enfeoffed Zhen'e as General of the Left and Inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu heard that Wang Zhen'e was dead, he submitted a memorial stating that "Shen Tianzi suddenly lost his mind and murdered a loyal servant of the state," and posthumously honored Zhen'e as General of the Left and Inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以彭城內史劉遵考為并州刺史、領河東太守，鎮蒲阪；

translations.literal: He appointed Liu Zunkao, Administrator of Pengcheng interior, as Inspector of Bingzhou and concurrent Administrator of Hedong, stationed at Puban;
translations.idiomatic: He made Liu Zunkao, Administrator of the Pengcheng interior, Inspector of Bingzhou and concurrent Administrator of Hedong, with his seat at Puban;

sentences.zh: 征荊州刺史劉道憐為徐、兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: and summoned Inspector of Jingzhou Liu Daolian to be Inspector of Xu and Yan provinces.
translations.idiomatic: and recalled Inspector of Jingzhou Liu Daolian to serve as Inspector of Xu and Yan.

sentences.zh: 裕欲以世子義符鎮荊州，以徐州刺史劉義隆為司州刺史，鎮洛陽。

translations.literal: Yu intended to station his heir Yifu as governor of Jingzhou and appoint Inspector of Xuzhou Liu Yilong as Inspector of Sizhou, stationed at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu planned to post his heir Yifu in Jingzhou and appoint Liu Yilong, Inspector of Xuzhou, as Inspector of Sizhou with his seat at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 中軍諮議張邵諫曰：「儲貳之重，四海所繫，不宜處外。

translations.literal: Central Army Adviser Zhang Shao remonstrated: "The weight of the heir-apparent binds the realm; he should not be placed outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Central Army Adviser Zhang Shao objected: "The heir-apparent is the linchpin of the empire. He must not be sent to govern a distant province.

sentences.zh: 」乃更以義隆為都督荊、益、寧、雍、梁、秦六州諸軍事、西中郎將、荊州刺史，以南郡太守到彥之為南蠻校尉，張邵為司馬、領南郡相，冠軍功曹王曇首為長史，北徐州從事王華為西中郎主簿，沈林子為西中郎參軍。

translations.literal: " He then changed the appointment and made Yilong Supervisor of Military Affairs for the six provinces of Jing, Yi, Ning, Yong, Liang, and Qin, General of the West, and Inspector of Jingzhou; Nanjun Administrator Dao Yanzhi was made Colonel of the Southern Barbarians; Zhang Shao became Major and concurrent Administrator of Nanjun; Champion Registrar Wang Tanshou became Chief Clerk; North Xuzhou staff officer Wang Hua became Secretariat of the General of the West; Shen Linzi became Adjutant of the General of the West.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu changed course. Liu Yilong was made Supervisor of Military Affairs for Jing, Yi, Ning, Yong, Liang, and Qin, General of the West, and Inspector of Jingzhou. Nanjun Administrator Dao Yanzhi became Colonel of the Southern Barbarians; Zhang Shao became Major and concurrent Administrator of Nanjun; Champion Registrar Wang Tanshou became Chief Clerk; North Xuzhou staff officer Wang Hua became Secretariat of the General of the West; and Shen Linzi became an adjutant on Yilong's staff.

sentences.zh: 義隆尚幼，府事皆決於邵。

translations.literal: Yilong was still young, and all office affairs were decided by Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong was still a boy, and every matter of the headquarters was decided by Shao.

sentences.zh: 曇首，弘之弟也。

translations.literal: Tanshou was Hongzhi's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Tanshou was Hongzhi's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 裕謂義隆曰：「王曇首沉毅有器度，宰相才也，汝每事咨之。

translations.literal: Yu told Yilong: "Wang Tanshou is steady, resolute, and magnanimous—talent fit for the chancellorship. Consult him on every matter.
translations.idiomatic: Yu told Yilong, "Wang Tanshou is deep, steady, and broad in spirit—material for a chief minister. Take counsel with him in all things.

sentences.zh: 以南郡公劉義慶為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Prince of Nanjun Liu Yiqing was appointed Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Nanjun Liu Yiqing was appointed Inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 義慶，道憐之子也。

translations.literal: Yiqing was Daolian's son.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing was Daolian's son.

sentences.zh: 裕解司州，領徐、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: Yu relinquished Sizhou and assumed concurrently the inspectorates of Xu and Ji provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Yu gave up Sizhou and took on the inspectorates of Xu and Ji in addition to his other duties.

sentences.zh: 秦王熾磐以乞伏木弈干為沙州刺史，鎮樂都。

translations.literal: King Chi Pan of Qin appointed Qifu Mugan as Inspector of Shazhou, stationed at Ledu.
translations.idiomatic: King Chi Pan of Qin appointed Qifu Mugan Inspector of Shazhou, with his headquarters at Ledu.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙弗烏地延帥戶二萬降秦。

translations.literal: In the second month, Bifu Wudiyan led twenty thousand households in surrendering to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Bifu Wudiyan brought twenty thousand households over to Qin in surrender.

sentences.zh: 三月，遣使聘魏。

translations.literal: In the third month, he sent envoys on a friendly visit to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he sent envoys to Wei on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己巳，魏徙冀、定、幽三州徒河於代都。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jisi, Wei moved the households relocated from Ji, Ding, and You provinces to the capital at Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month on jisi, Wei transferred the resettled populations of Ji, Ding, and You to the capital at Dai.

sentences.zh: 初，和龍有赤氣四塞蔽日，自寅至申，燕太史令張穆言於燕王跋曰：「此兵氣也。

translations.literal: Earlier, at Helong crimson vapors filled every quarter and blotted out the sun from yin to shen hours; Yan Grand Astrologer Zhang Mu told King Ba of Yan: "This is the breath of war.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier at Helong, red mists had filled the sky and blocked out the sun from dawn till mid-afternoon. Yan Grand Astrologer Zhang Mu told King Ba, "This is the aura of war.

sentences.zh: 今魏方強盛，而執其使者，好命不通，臣竊懼焉。

translations.literal: Wei is now strong and flourishing, yet we detain their envoy and no cordial messages pass between us—I am privately afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Wei grows stronger by the day, yet we hold their envoy and no friendly word passes between us. I fear what may follow.

sentences.zh: 」跋曰：「吾方思之。

translations.literal: " Ba said: "I am considering this now.
translations.idiomatic: " Ba said, "I have been thinking the same.

sentences.zh: 」五月，魏主嗣東巡，至濡源及甘松，遣征東將軍長孫道生、安東將軍李先、給事黃門侍郎奚觀帥精騎二萬襲燕，又命驍騎將軍延普、幽州刺史尉諾自幽州引兵趨遼西，為之聲勢，嗣屯突門嶺以待之。

translations.literal: " In the fifth month, Emperor Si of Wei toured east to Ruyuan and Gansong, sent Campaigning-East General Zhangsun Daosheng, Pacifying-the-East General Li Xian, and Yellow Gate Attendant Xi Guan leading twenty thousand elite cavalry to raid Yan, and also ordered Fierce Cavalry General Yan Pu and Inspector of Youzhou Wei Nuo to lead troops from Youzhou toward Liaoxi to create a demonstration of force, while Si encamped at Tumen Ridge to await results.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth month Emperor Si of Wei toured east as far as Ruyuan and Gansong. He sent Campaigning-East General Zhangsun Daosheng, Pacifying-the-East General Li Xian, and Yellow Gate Attendant Xi Guan at the head of twenty thousand picked horsemen to strike Yan, and ordered Fierce Cavalry General Yan Pu and Inspector of Youzhou Wei Nuo to march from Youzhou into Liaoxi to lend weight to the attack, while Si himself waited at Tumen Ridge.

sentences.zh: 道生等拔乙連城，進攻和龍，與燕單于右輔古泥戰，破之，殺其將皇甫軌。

translations.literal: Daosheng and the others captured Yilian Fortress, advanced to attack Helong, fought Right Assistant Guni of the Yan Xiongnu chieftain, defeated him, and killed his general Huangfu Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng and his commanders took Yilian Fortress, pressed on against Helong, fought Yan's Right Assistant Guni, routed him, and killed his general Huangfu Gui.

sentences.zh: 燕王跋嬰城自守，魏人攻之，不克，掠其民萬餘家而還。

translations.literal: King Ba of Yan tied himself to the city in defense; the Wei troops attacked but could not take it, carried off more than ten thousand of his people, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: King Ba barricaded himself inside Helong. The Wei army could not breach the walls, so it carried off more than ten thousand of his people and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 六月，太尉裕始受相國、宋公、九錫之命。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Grand Marshal Yu first received the appointments of Chancellor, Duke of Song, and the Nine Bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Grand Marshal Yu at last accepted the titles of Chancellor, Duke of Song, and the Nine Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 赦國中殊死以下，崇繼母蘭陵蕭氏為太妃。

translations.literal: He pardoned all crimes below capital offense throughout the state and exalted his stepmother, Lady Xiao of Lanling, as Grand Consort.
translations.idiomatic: He granted amnesty for all offenses short of capital crime throughout the realm and raised his stepmother, Lady Xiao of Lanling, to the rank of Grand Consort.

sentences.zh: 以太尉軍諮祭酒孔靖為宋國尚書令，左長史王弘為僕射，領選，從事中郎傅亮、蔡廓皆為侍中，謝晦為右衛將軍，右長史鄭鮮之為奉常，行參軍殷景仁為秘書郎，其餘百官，悉依天朝之制。

translations.literal: He appointed Grand Marshal Military Staff Sacrificer Kong Jing as Director of the Masters of Writing of the State of Song, Left Chief Clerk Wang Hong as Vice Director with charge of selection, Staff Officers Fu Liang and Cai Kuo both as Palace Attendants, Xie Hui as General of the Right Guard, Right Chief Clerk Zheng Xianzhi as Director of Ceremonies, Acting Adjutant Yin Jingren as Secretariat Gentleman—the rest of the officials all following the imperial court's system.
translations.idiomatic: He named Grand Marshal Military Staff Sacrificer Kong Jing Director of the Masters of Writing of Song, Left Chief Clerk Wang Hong Vice Director with charge of appointments, Staff Officers Fu Liang and Cai Kuo Palace Attendants, Xie Hui General of the Right Guard, Right Chief Clerk Zheng Xianzhi Director of Ceremonies, and Acting Adjutant Yin Jingren Secretariat Gentleman; the remaining offices were filled according to the imperial model.

sentences.zh: 靖辭不受。

translations.literal: Jing declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Jing refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 亮，鹹之孫；

translations.literal: Liang was Xian's grandson;
translations.idiomatic: Liang was a grandson of Xian;

sentences.zh: 廓，謨之曾孫；

translations.literal: Kuo was Mo's great-grandson;
translations.idiomatic: Kuo was a great-grandson of Mo;

sentences.zh: 鮮之，渾之玄孫；

translations.literal: Xianzhi was Hun's great-great-grandson;
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi was a great-great-grandson of Hun;

sentences.zh: 景仁，融之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Jingren was Rong's great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: and Jingren was a great-grandson of Rong.

sentences.zh: 景仁學不為文，敏有思致；

translations.literal: Jingren did not pursue literary composition but was quick and thoughtful;
translations.idiomatic: Jingren cared little for polished prose, yet he was quick-witted and penetrating;

sentences.zh: 口不談義，深達理體；

translations.literal: he did not discourse on abstruse doctrine yet deeply grasped principle;
translations.idiomatic: he never lectured on metaphysics, yet he understood the heart of affairs;

sentences.zh: 至於國典、朝儀、舊章、記注，莫不撰錄，識者知其有當世之志。

translations.literal: as for state statutes, court ritual, old regulations, and historical records, there was nothing he did not compile—and perceptive men knew he harbored ambition for his age.
translations.idiomatic: and whether the topic was state law, court ceremony, ancient precedent, or historical record, there was scarcely a document he had not gathered and annotated. Those who knew him saw in this the ambition of a man meant for power.

sentences.zh: 魏天部大人白馬文貞公崔宏疾篤，魏主嗣遣侍臣問病，一夜數返。

translations.literal: Cui Hong, Great Man of the Heavenly Division and Duke Wen of White Horse, lay gravely ill; Emperor Si of Wei sent palace attendants to inquire after his health, returning several times in a single night.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hong, Great Man of the Heavenly Division and Duke Wen of White Horse, lay near death. Emperor Si sent courtiers to ask after him, and they came and went several times in one night.

sentences.zh: 及卒，詔群臣及附國渠帥皆會葬。

translations.literal: When he died, an edict summoned all ministers and chieftains of subject peoples to gather for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, an edict ordered every minister and every chieftain of the subject tribes to attend the burial.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊午，魏主嗣至平城。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuwu, Emperor Si of Wei reached Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month on wuwu, Emperor Si of Wei arrived at Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲寅，魏人命諸州調民租，戶五十石，積於定、相、冀三州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jiayin, Wei ordered the provinces to levy grain rents from the people—fifty piculs per household—stored up in Ding, Xiang, and Ji provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month on jiayin Wei ordered every province to levy fifty piculs of grain rent per household and stockpile it in Ding, Xiang, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 河西王蒙遜復引兵伐涼，涼公歆將拒之，左長史張體順固諫，乃止。

translations.literal: King Mengsun of Hexi again led troops to attack Liang; Duke of Liang Xin was about to resist, but Left Chief Clerk Zhang Tishun firmly remonstrated and he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: King Mengsun of Hexi marched against Liang again. Duke of Liang Xin prepared to meet him in battle, but Left Chief Clerk Zhang Tishun pleaded against it until he gave up the idea.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜芟其秋稼而還。

translations.literal: Mengsun mowed down their autumn crops and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Mengsun cut down their autumn grain and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 歆遣使來告襲位。

translations.literal: Xin sent envoys to report his succession.
translations.idiomatic: Xin sent envoys to announce that he had taken the throne.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，以歆為都督七郡諸軍事、鎮西大將軍、酒泉公。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Xin was appointed Supervisor of Military Affairs for seven commanderies, General Who Pacifies the West, and Duke of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Xin was made Supervisor of Military Affairs for seven commanderies, General Who Pacifies the West, and Duke of Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 姚艾叛秦，降河西王蒙遜，蒙遜引兵迎之。

translations.literal: Yao Ai rebelled against Qin, surrendered to King Mengsun of Hexi, and Mengsun led troops to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Ai rebelled against Qin and went over to King Mengsun of Hexi, who marched out to receive him.

sentences.zh: 艾叔父俊言於眾曰：「秦王寬仁有雅度，自可安居事之，何為從河西王西遷！

translations.literal: Yao Ai's uncle Jun addressed the gathering: "The King of Qin is generous, benevolent, and magnanimous—one can live in peace serving him. Why follow the King of Hexi west in exile!
translations.idiomatic: Yao Ai's uncle Jun told the people, "The King of Qin is generous and steady of mind. Under him we can live in peace. Why follow the King of Hexi into exile in the west!

sentences.zh: 」眾鹹以為然，乃相與逐艾，推俊為主，復歸於秦。

translations.literal: " The crowd all agreed; they drove Ai out together, made Jun their leader, and returned to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: " The people agreed. They drove Ai out, made Jun their leader, and returned to Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦王熾磐征俊為侍中、中書監、征南將軍，賜爵隴西公，以左丞相曇達為都督洮、罕以東諸軍事、征東大將軍、秦州牧，鎮南安。

translations.literal: King Chi Pan of Qin summoned Jun as Palace Attendant, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, General Who Campaigns South, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Longxi; Left Chancellor Tanda was made Supervisor of Military Affairs east of Tao and Han, General Who Campaigns East, and Governor of Qinzhou, stationed at Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: King Chi Pan summoned Jun as Palace Attendant, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and General Who Campaigns South, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Longxi. Left Chancellor Tanda was made Supervisor of Military Affairs east of Tao and Han, General Who Campaigns East, and Governor of Qinzhou, with his seat at Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 劉義真年少，賜與左右無節，王修每裁抑之。

translations.literal: Liu Yizhen was young and gave presents to his attendants without restraint; Wang Xiu constantly checked and restrained him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yizhen was still young and showered his attendants with gifts without limit. Wang Xiu checked him at every turn.

sentences.zh: 左右皆怨，譖修於義真曰：「王鎮惡欲反，故沈田子殺之。

translations.literal: The attendants all resented this and slandered Xiu to Yizhen: "Wang Zhen'e intended to rebel, so Shen Tianzi killed him.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants nursed their resentment and whispered to Yizhen, "Wang Zhen'e meant to rebel, and that is why Shen Tianzi killed him.

sentences.zh: 修殺田子，是亦欲反也。

translations.literal: Xiu killed Tianzi—he too intends to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu killed Tianzi—he means to rebel as well.

sentences.zh: 」義真信之，使左右劉乞等殺修。

translations.literal: " Yizhen believed them and had his attendants Liu Qi and others kill Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: " Yizhen believed them and sent Liu Qi and the other attendants to kill Xiu.

sentences.zh: 修既死，人情離駭，莫相統壹。

translations.literal: Once Xiu was dead, hearts scattered in alarm and no one held command together.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu was dead, morale collapsed. No one could hold the army together.

sentences.zh: 義真悉召外軍入長安，閉門拒守。

translations.literal: Yizhen summoned all outside troops into Chang'an, shut the gates, and held the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen called every outside garrison into Chang'an, shut the gates, and prepared to defend the city.

sentences.zh: 關中郡縣悉降於夏。

translations.literal: All commanderies and counties of Guanzhong surrendered to Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Every commandery and county in Guanzhong submitted to Xia.

sentences.zh: 赫連瑰夜襲長安，不克，夏王勃勃進據咸陽，長安樵采路絕。

translations.literal: Helian Gui raided Chang'an by night but could not take it; King Bobo of Xia advanced to occupy Xianyang, and the roads for firewood-gathering around Chang'an were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Gui struck Chang'an by night but failed to take it. King Bobo of Xia pressed forward to occupy Xianyang, and the paths by which Chang'an gathered firewood were severed.

sentences.zh: 宋公裕聞之，使輔國將軍蒯恩如長安，召義真東歸；

translations.literal: When Duke Yu of Song heard this, he sent Assisting-the-State General Kuai En to Chang'an to summon Yizhen east;
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Yu of Song heard what had happened, he sent Assisting-the-State General Kuai En to Chang'an to bring Yizhen home;

sentences.zh: 以相國右司馬朱齡石為都督關中諸軍事、右將軍、雍州刺史，代鎮長安。

translations.literal: he appointed Chancellor's Right Major Zhu Lingshi as Supervisor of Military Affairs in Guanzhong, General of the Right, and Inspector of Yongzhou to replace Yizhen in holding Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: he appointed Chancellor's Right Major Zhu Lingshi Supervisor of Military Affairs in Guanzhong, General of the Right, and Inspector of Yongzhou to hold Chang'an in Yizhen's place.

sentences.zh: 裕謂齡石曰：「卿至，可敕義真輕裝速發，既出關，然後可徐行。

translations.literal: Yu told Lingshi: "When you arrive, order Yizhen to travel light and depart swiftly; only after he has cleared the passes may he proceed at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Yu told Lingshi, "When you arrive, tell Yizhen to strip down and move fast. Only after he is out of the passes may he take his time.

sentences.zh: 若關右必不可守，可與義真俱歸。

translations.literal: If Guanxi cannot be held at all, you may return together with Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: If the west cannot be held at all, come back with him.

sentences.zh: 」又命中書侍郎朱超石慰勞河、洛。

translations.literal: " He also ordered Secretariat Attendant Zhu Chaoshi to console the regions of the Yellow River and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: " He also ordered Secretariat Attendant Zhu Chaoshi to reassure the people along the Yellow River and in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十一月，齡石至長安。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Lingshi reached Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Lingshi reached Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 義真將士貪縱，大掠而東，多載寶貨、子女，方軌徐行。

translations.literal: Yizhen's officers and soldiers, greedy and unrestrained, looted on a great scale as they marched east, laden with treasure, goods, and women, traveling in parallel columns at a leisurely pace.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen's officers and men, drunk on greed, plundered as they went east, loading wagons with gold, goods, and captive women and marching in wide columns at a crawl.

sentences.zh: 雍州別駕韋華奔夏，赫連瑰帥眾三萬追義真。

translations.literal: Yongzhou Attendant Counsel Wei Hua fled to Xia; Helian Gui led thirty thousand men in pursuit of Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhou Attendant Counsel Wei Hua defected to Xia. Helian Gui came after Yizhen with thirty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 建威將軍傅弘之曰：「公處分亟進；

translations.literal: Establishing-Might General Fu Hongzhi said: "Our lord ordered a swift advance;
translations.idiomatic: Establishing-Might General Fu Hongzhi said, "Our lord ordered us to move quickly;

sentences.zh: 今多將輜重，一日行不過十里，虜追騎且至，何以待之！

translations.literal: now we are burdened with wagons and baggage and advance no more than ten li a day—the enemy's cavalry will soon arrive. What then shall we do!
translations.idiomatic: yet we are dragging a train of wagons and cover barely ten li a day. The enemy cavalry will be on us soon. What then!

sentences.zh: 宜棄車輕行，乃可以免。

translations.literal: We ought to abandon the carts and travel light—that alone can save us.
translations.idiomatic: Cast off the wagons and travel light—that is the only way out.

sentences.zh: 」義真不從。

translations.literal: " Yizhen would not heed this.
translations.idiomatic: " Yizhen would not listen.

sentences.zh: 俄而夏兵大至，傅弘之、蒯恩斷後，力戰連日，至青泥，晉兵大敗，弘之、恩皆為王買德所禽。

translations.literal: Before long the Xia army arrived in force; Fu Hongzhi and Kuai En covered the retreat and fought fiercely for days. At Qingni the Jin troops suffered a great defeat; Hongzhi and En were both captured by Wang Maide.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Xia army closed in. Fu Hongzhi and Kuai En held the rear and fought day after day. At Qingni the Jin force was shattered. Hongzhi and En were both taken by Wang Maide.

sentences.zh: 司馬毛修之與義真相失，亦為夏兵所禽。

translations.literal: Major Mao Xiuzhi lost contact with Yizhen and was also captured by Xia troops.
translations.idiomatic: Major Mao Xiuzhi lost Yizhen in the rout and was captured as well.

sentences.zh: 義真行在前，會日暮，夏兵不窮追，故得免；

translations.literal: Yizhen was marching in front; as night fell the Xia troops did not press the pursuit, and so he escaped;
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen had gone on ahead. Night fell, the Xia pursuers slackened, and he slipped away;

sentences.zh: 左右盡散，獨逃草中。

translations.literal: his attendants all scattered, and he fled alone into the grass.
translations.idiomatic: his attendants had all fled, and he hid alone in the tall grass.

sentences.zh: 中兵參軍段宏單騎追尋，緣道呼之，義真識其聲，出就之，曰：「君非段中兵邪？

translations.literal: Staff Officer of the Central Army Duan Hong rode alone in search along the road, calling out; Yizhen recognized his voice, emerged to meet him, and said: "Are you not Staff Officer Duan?
translations.idiomatic: Staff Officer of the Central Army Duan Hong rode alone along the road calling his name. Yizhen knew the voice, came out of hiding, and said, "Is that you, Staff Officer Duan?

sentences.zh: 身在此，行矣！

translations.literal: I am here—go on!
translations.idiomatic: I am here. Go on!

sentences.zh: 必不兩全，可刎身頭以南，使家公望絕。

translations.literal: We cannot both survive. You may cut off my head and carry it south, so that my father's hopes are ended.
translations.idiomatic: We cannot both live. Cut off my head and carry it south, so my father's line ends with me.

sentences.zh: 」宏泣曰：「今日之事，誠無算略；

translations.literal: " Hong wept and said: "Today's affair truly admits no stratagem;
translations.idiomatic: " Hong wept and said, "There is no clever plan that can save us today;

sentences.zh: 然丈夫不經此，何以知艱難！

translations.literal: yet what man, without passing through this, can know hardship!
translations.idiomatic: but what man ever learned what hardship means without passing through a day like this!

sentences.zh: 夏王勃勃欲降傅弘之，弘之不屈。

translations.literal: King Bobo of Xia wished to win Fu Hongzhi over; Hongzhi would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: King Bobo of Xia tried to win Fu Hongzhi over. Hongzhi refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 時天寒，勃勃裸之，弘之叫罵而死。

translations.literal: It was bitterly cold; Bobo stripped him naked, and Hongzhi died shouting curses.
translations.idiomatic: The weather was freezing. Bobo had him stripped bare, and Hongzhi died cursing him to the last.

sentences.zh: 勃勃積人頭為京觀，號曰髑髏台。

translations.literal: Bobo piled up human heads into a victory mound and called it the Skull Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo heaped the slain into a mound of skulls and named it the Terrace of Bones.

sentences.zh: 長安百姓逐朱齡石，齡石焚其宮殿，奔潼關。

translations.literal: The people of Chang'an drove out Zhu Lingshi; Lingshi burned the palace buildings and fled to Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chang'an turned on Zhu Lingshi. He set the palace afire and fled toward Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 勃勃入長安，大饗將士，舉觴謂王買德曰：「卿往日之言，一期而驗，可謂算無遺策。

translations.literal: Bobo entered Chang'an, feasted his officers and soldiers, raised his cup, and said to Wang Maide: "Your words of other days have been vindicated in a single season—truly your calculations left nothing out.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo entered Chang'an and feasted his army. Raising his cup to Wang Maide he said, "What you foretold has come true in a single season. Not one stroke of your planning was wasted.

sentences.zh: 此觴所集，非卿而誰！

translations.literal: This cup I raise—if not for you, then for whom!
translations.idiomatic: This toast is yours and no one else's!

sentences.zh: 」以買德為都官尚書，封河陽候。

translations.literal: " He made Maide Director of the Masters of Writing for Punishments and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: " He made Maide Director of the Masters of Writing for Punishments and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍王敬先戍曹公壘，齡石往從之。

translations.literal: Flying-Dragon General Wang Jingxian garrisoned Duke Cao's Fortress; Lingshi went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Flying-Dragon General Wang Jingxian held Duke Cao's Fortress, and Lingshi went to join him there.

sentences.zh: 朱超石至蒲阪，聞齡石所在，亦往從之。

translations.literal: Zhu Chaoshi reached Puban; hearing where Lingshi was, he went to join him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Chaoshi reached Puban, learned where Lingshi was, and went to join him.

sentences.zh: 赫連昌攻敬先壘，斷其水道。

translations.literal: Helian Chang attacked Jingxian's fortress and cut off its water supply.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Chang besieged Jingxian's fort and cut off its water.

sentences.zh: 眾渴，不能戰，城且陷。

translations.literal: The men were parched, could not fight, and the city was on the verge of falling.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison thirsted, could no longer fight, and the fort was near collapse.

sentences.zh: 齡石謂超石曰：「弟兄俱死異城，使老親何以為心！

translations.literal: Lingshi said to Chaoshi: "If both brothers die in separate cities, what will become of our aged parents' hearts!
translations.idiomatic: Lingshi told Chaoshi, "If both brothers die in different cities, what will become of our old parents!

sentences.zh: 爾求間道亡歸，我死此，無恨矣。

translations.literal: You find a secret path and flee home—I die here without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Find a way out and go home. I will die here without regret.

sentences.zh: 」超石持兄泣曰：「人誰不死，寧忍今日辭兄去乎！

translations.literal: " Chaoshi clutched his brother and wept: "Who among men does not die? How could I bear to leave my brother today!
translations.idiomatic: " Chaoshi seized his brother's arm and wept, "All men must die. How could I leave you today!

sentences.zh: 」遂與敬先及右軍參軍劉欽之皆被執，送長安，勃勃殺之；

translations.literal: " In the end Jingxian, Adjutant of the Right Army Liu Qinzhi, and the others were all seized, sent to Chang'an, and executed by Bobo;
translations.idiomatic: " In the end Jingxian, Adjutant of the Right Army Liu Qinzhi, and the rest were taken, sent to Chang'an, and put to death by Bobo;

sentences.zh: 欽之弟秀之悲泣不歡燕者十年。

translations.literal: Qinzhi's younger brother Xiuzhi grieved and wept, finding no joy in feasting, for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhi's younger brother Xiuzhi mourned so deeply that for ten years he could find no pleasure even at a feast.

sentences.zh: 欽之，穆之之從兄子也。

translations.literal: Qinzhi was a son of Muzhi's older cousin brother.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhi was the son of Muzhi's elder cousin.

sentences.zh: 宋公裕聞青泥敗，未知義真存亡，怒甚，刻日北伐，侍中謝晦諫以「士卒疲弊，請俟它年」，不從。

translations.literal: Duke Yu of Song heard of the defeat at Qingni, not knowing whether Yizhen was alive or dead; he was extremely angered, set a date for a northern campaign, and Palace Attendant Xie Hui remonstrated saying, "The soldiers are exhausted and debilitated; please wait until another year"—he did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Yu of Song heard of the defeat at Qingni and did not know whether Yizhen still lived, he was furious and fixed a day for a northern expedition. Palace Attendant Xie Hui urged that the troops were worn out and asked him to wait another year, but Yu would not listen.

sentences.zh: 鄭鮮之上表，以為：「虜聞殿下親征，必並力守潼關。

translations.literal: Zheng Xianzhi submitted a memorial, saying: "When the enemy hears that Your Highness will personally campaign, they will surely combine their strength to defend Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xianzhi submitted a memorial stating, "When the barbarians hear that Your Highness will take the field in person, they will surely concentrate all their forces to hold Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 徑往攻之，恐未易可克；

translations.literal: If one goes straight to attack them, I fear it will not be easy to overcome;
translations.idiomatic: A direct assault may not be easy to succeed.

sentences.zh: 若輿駕頓洛，則不足上勞聖躬。

translations.literal: If the imperial carriage halts at Luoyang, it is not worth the trouble of exhausting Your Sacred Person on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: If the imperial retinue halts at Luoyang, it would hardly be worth troubling Your Majesty to make the journey.

sentences.zh: 且虜雖得志，不敢乘勝過關陝者，猶懾服大威，為將來之慮故也。

translations.literal: Moreover, though the enemy has gained their aim, the reason they dare not press their victory and cross Pass Shan is that they still fear and submit to our great majesty, taking thought for future consequences.
translations.idiomatic: Though the enemy has won their objective, they dare not follow up their victory and cross into the passes of Shan because they still stand in awe of our might and are thinking of what may come next.

sentences.zh: 若造洛而返，虜必更有揣量之心，或益生邊患。

translations.literal: If we go as far as Luoyang and then return, the enemy will surely become more calculating in mind, and border troubles may even increase.
translations.idiomatic: If we reach Luoyang only to turn back, the enemy will read that as hesitation and border troubles may grow worse.

sentences.zh: 況大軍遠出，後患甚多。

translations.literal: Moreover, when a great army marches far abroad, the troubles afterward are many.
translations.idiomatic: And when a large army campaigns far from home, the after-effects are seldom small.

sentences.zh: 昔歲西征，劉鐘狼狽；

translations.literal: In the western expedition of the previous year, Liu Zhong was thrown into disarray;
translations.idiomatic: Last year's western campaign ended with Liu Zhong in disarray;

sentences.zh: 去年北討，廣州傾覆；

translations.literal: Last year's northern expedition saw Guang Province overturned;
translations.idiomatic: The northern expedition the year before brought catastrophe to Guang Province;

sentences.zh: 既往之效，後來之鑒也。

translations.literal: The outcomes of the past are a mirror for what is to come.
translations.idiomatic: Past results are a lesson for the future.

sentences.zh: 今諸州大水，民食寡乏，三吳群盜攻沒諸縣，皆由困於征役故也。

translations.literal: Now the provinces have suffered great floods, the people's food is scarce, and the bandits of the Three Wu regions have attacked and overrun counties—all because they are exhausted by corvée and military service.
translations.idiomatic: Floods have struck many provinces, food is scarce, and bandits in the Three Wu region are overrunning county after county—all because the people are worn down by levies and conscription.

sentences.zh: 江南士庶，引領顒顒以望殿下之返旆，聞更北出，不測淺深之謀，往還之期，臣恐返顧之憂更在腹心也。

translations.literal: The gentry and commoners of the Jiangnan region stretch their necks and gaze eagerly, awaiting Your Highness's returning banner; hearing that you will campaign north again, not knowing the depth of the plan or the time of going and returning, your servant fears that the worry of turning back to look will lie even nearer at the heart.
translations.idiomatic: The people south of the Yangzi are straining to see Your Highness return; if they learn you mean to march north again, not knowing how deep the plan goes or when you will come back, I fear the danger you leave behind at home may prove worse than any on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 若慮西虜更為河、洛之患者，宜結好北虜；

translations.literal: If you worry that the Western Barbarians will again bring trouble to the He and Luo region, you should make friendly ties with the Northern Barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: If you fear further trouble in the He-Luo region from the Western foe, you should seek an alliance with the Northern barbarians;

sentences.zh: 北虜親則河南安，河南安則濟、泗靜矣。

translations.literal: If the Northern Barbarians are friendly, then Henan will be secure; if Henan is secure, then Ji and Si will be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: With the northerners bound to us in friendship, the lands south of the Yellow River will be secure—and once Henan is secure, Ji and Si will be quiet.

sentences.zh: 」會得段宏啟，知義真得免，裕乃止，但登城北望，慨然流涕而已。

translations.literal: " It happened that a dispatch from Duan Hong was received, letting them know Yizhen had escaped; Yu thereupon stopped, but only climbed the city wall and looked north, sighing with tears—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: " Then a report from Duan Hong arrived confirming that Yizhen had escaped alive. Yu called off the campaign and merely climbed the city wall to gaze northward, weeping in grief.

sentences.zh: 降義真為建威將軍、司州刺史；

translations.literal: Yizhen was demoted to General Establishing Might and Inspector of Si Province;
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen was demoted to General Establishing Might and made Inspector of Si Province;

sentences.zh: 以段宏為宋台黃門郎、領太子右衛率。

translations.literal: Duan Hong was made Yellow Gate Gentleman of the Song court and concurrently commander of the Crown Prince's Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Hong was appointed Yellow Gate Gentleman of the Song court and put in charge of the Crown Prince's Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 裕以天水太守毛德祖為河東太守，代劉遵考守蒲阪。

translations.literal: Yu made Mao Dezu, Administrator of Tianshui, Administrator of Hedong, replacing Liu Zunkao in garrisoning Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Yu appointed Mao Dezu, Administrator of Tianshui, as Administrator of Hedong to replace Liu Zunkao in holding Puban.

sentences.zh: 夏王勃勃築壇於灞上，即皇帝位，改元昌武。

translations.literal: Xia King Bobo erected an altar at Bashang, ascended the imperial throne, and changed the era name to Changwu.
translations.idiomatic: Xia King Bobo built an altar at Bashang, took the imperial throne, and proclaimed the era name Changwu.

sentences.zh: 西秦王熾磐東巡；

translations.literal: Western Qin King Qifu Chipan toured eastward;
translations.idiomatic: Western Qin King Qifu Chipan made an eastern tour;

sentences.zh: 十二月，徙上邽民五千餘戶於枹罕。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, he moved more than five thousand households of the people of Shanggui to Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he relocated more than five thousand households from Shanggui to Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 彗星出天津，入太微，經北斗，絡紫微，八十餘日而滅。

translations.literal: A comet emerged at Tianjin, entered Taiwei, passed through the Northern Dipper, connected with Ziwei, and vanished after more than eighty days.
translations.idiomatic: A comet appeared at Tianjin, entered Taiwei, passed through the Northern Dipper, linked with Ziwei, and disappeared after more than eighty days.

sentences.zh: 魏主嗣復召諸儒、術土問之曰：「今四海分裂，災咎之應，果在何國？

translations.literal: The Wei ruler Si again summoned the Confucian scholars and occultists and asked them: "Now the realm is divided in four, and calamitous portents have appeared—in which state do they truly fall?
translations.idiomatic: Wei ruler Si again summoned the Confucian scholars and occult specialists and asked, "The realm is now split in four—where do these calamitous signs truly fall?

sentences.zh: 騰甚畏之。

translations.literal: Its flight is greatly to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Its soaring course inspires great fear.

sentences.zh: 卿輩盡言，勿有所隱！

translations.literal: You all speak fully—hide nothing!
translations.idiomatic: Speak freely, and hide nothing!

sentences.zh: 」眾推崔浩使對，浩曰：「夫災異之興，皆像人事，人苟無釁，又何畏焉？

translations.literal: " The assembly pushed forward Cui Hao to answer. Hao said: "When strange calamities arise, they all mirror human affairs; if men have no fault, what is there to fear?
translations.idiomatic: " The group put forward Cui Hao to reply. Hao said, "Strange portents arise because they reflect human affairs. If people are without guilt, what is there to fear?

sentences.zh: 昔王莽將篡漢，彗星出入，正與今同。

translations.literal: In the past, when Wang Mang was about to usurp Han, a comet appeared and departed in just the same way as today.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mang was about to usurp the Han throne, a comet moved in and out in exactly the same way as now.

sentences.zh: 國家主尊臣卑，民無異望，晉室陵夷，危亡不遠；

translations.literal: In our state the ruler is honored and ministers subordinate, the people have no other expectations; the Jin house is in decline, danger and ruin not far off;
translations.idiomatic: In our state the ruler is honored and ministers are humble, the people have no other hopes, and the Jin house is sinking toward ruin;

sentences.zh: 彗之為異，其劉裕將篡之應乎！

translations.literal: Is not this comet's strange sign the omen of Liu Yu's impending usurpation!
translations.idiomatic: Is this comet not the sign that Liu Yu is about to usurp the throne!

sentences.zh: 」眾無以易其言。

translations.literal: " No one could refute his words.
translations.idiomatic: " No one could dispute what he said.

sentences.zh: 宋公裕以讖云「昌明之後尚有二帝」，乃使中書侍郎王韶之與帝左右密謀鴆帝而立琅邪王德文。

translations.literal: Duke Yu of Song, because a prophecy said "After Changming there are still two emperors," had Palace Secretariat Attendant Wang Shaozhi secretly plot with the emperor's attendants to poison the emperor and set up Langye Wang Dewen.
translations.idiomatic: Because a prophecy read "After Changming there are still two emperors," Duke Yu of Song had Palace Secretariat Attendant Wang Shaozhi secretly conspire with the emperor's attendants to poison the emperor and install Langye Wang Dewen.

sentences.zh: 德文常在帝左右，飲食寢處，未嘗暫離；

translations.literal: Dewen was constantly at the emperor's side in eating, drinking, and sleeping—never briefly parted;
translations.idiomatic: Dewen was always at the emperor's side for meals and sleep and never left him for a moment;

sentences.zh: 韶之伺之經時，不得間。

translations.literal: Shaozhi watched for a long time but found no opening.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozhi watched for a long time but never found an opportunity.

sentences.zh: 會德文有疾，出居於外。

translations.literal: When Dewen fell ill and went out to live elsewhere,
translations.idiomatic: When Dewen fell ill and moved out to convalesce elsewhere,

sentences.zh: 戊寅，韶之以散衣縊帝於東堂。

translations.literal: On day wuyin, Shaozhi strangled the emperor in the Eastern Hall with a loose garment.
translations.idiomatic: On day wuyin, Shaozhi strangled the emperor in the Eastern Hall with a loose garment.

sentences.zh: 韶之，廙之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Shaozhi was a great-grandson of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozhi was a great-grandson of Yi.

sentences.zh: 裕因稱遺詔，奉德文即皇帝位，大赦。

translations.literal: Yu thereupon claimed a testamentary edict, installed Dewen as emperor, and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Yu then claimed a deathbed edict, enthroned Dewen as emperor, and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 是歲，河西王蒙遜奉表稱籓，拜涼州刺史。

translations.literal: That year, Hexi King Mengsun submitted a memorial declaring himself a vassal and was appointed Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Hexi King Mengsun submitted a memorial acknowledging vassal status and was appointed Governor of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射袁湛卒。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Zhan died.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Zhan died.

sentences.zh: 恭皇帝

translations.literal: Emperor Gong
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gong

sentences.zh: 安皇帝癸元熙元年（

translations.literal: First year of Yuanxi of Emperor An, guǐ (
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanxi during the reign of Emperor An (

sentences.zh: 己未，公元四一九年）

translations.literal: jiwei, corresponding to CE 419)
translations.idiomatic: jiwei, corresponding to CE 419)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬辰朔，改元。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on renchen the first day of the month, the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on renchen the first day of the month, the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 立琅邪王紀褚氏為皇后；

translations.literal: Langye Wang Lady Ji Chu was made empress;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ji Chu of Langye was made empress;

sentences.zh: 後，裒之曾孫也。

translations.literal: The empress was a great-granddaughter of Bao.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was a great-granddaughter of Bao.

sentences.zh: 魏主嗣畋於犢渚。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler Si hunted at Duzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei ruler Si went hunting at Duzhu.

sentences.zh: 甲午，征宋公裕入朝，進爵為王。

translations.literal: On day jiawu, Duke Yu of Song was summoned to court and promoted in rank to prince.
translations.idiomatic: On day jiawu, Duke Yu of Song was summoned to court and promoted to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 裕辭。

translations.literal: Yu declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yu declined.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，魏主嗣還平城。

translations.literal: On day guimao, the Wei ruler Si returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On day guimao, Wei ruler Si returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 庚申，葬安皇帝於休平陵。

translations.literal: On day gengshen, Emperor An was buried at Xiuping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On day gengshen, Emperor An was buried at Xiuping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 敕劉道憐司空出鎮京口。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Liu Daolian, Minister of Works, to go out and garrison Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Liu Daolian, Minister of Works, to leave the capital and garrison Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 夏將叱奴侯提帥步騎二萬攻毛德祖於蒲阪，德祖不能御，全軍歸彭城。

translations.literal: Xia General Chinu Houti led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Mao Dezu at Puban; Dezu could not withstand him and returned with his whole army to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xia General Chinu Houti led twenty thousand foot and horse soldiers against Mao Dezu at Puban. Dezu could not hold and withdrew his entire force to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 二月，宋公裕以德祖為滎陽太守，戍虎牢。

translations.literal: In the second month, Duke Yu of Song made Dezu Administrator of Xingyang to garrison Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Duke Yu of Song appointed Dezu Administrator of Xingyang and posted him to garrison Hulao.

sentences.zh: 夏主勃勃征隱土京兆韋祖思。

translations.literal: Xia Emperor Bobo summoned the recluse Wei Zusi of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Emperor Bobo summoned the recluse Wei Zusi of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖思既至，恭懼過甚，勃勃怒曰：「我以國士征汝，汝乃以非類遇我，汝昔不拜姚興，今何獨拜我？

translations.literal: When Zusi arrived, his excessive reverence and fear enraged Bobo, who said: "I summoned you as a worthy of the realm—yet you treat me like an alien! In the past you would not bow to Yao Xing; why do you bow to me alone now?
translations.idiomatic: When Zusi arrived, his excessive deference and fear enraged Bobo, who said, "I summoned you as a man of the realm, yet you treat me as something other! You would not bow to Yao Xing before—why do you bow to me alone now?

sentences.zh: 我在，汝猶不以我為帝王；

translations.literal: While I live, you still do not regard me as an emperor;
translations.idiomatic: While I am alive, you still do not treat me as an emperor;

sentences.zh: 我死，汝曹弄筆，當置我於何地邪！

translations.literal: After I die, you lot wield your pens—where will you place me then!
translations.idiomatic: After I die, you scribblers with your brushes—where will you put me then!

sentences.zh: 遂殺之。

translations.literal: He then had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: He then had him killed.

sentences.zh: 群臣請都長安，勃勃曰：「朕豈不知長安歷世帝王之都，沃饒險固！

translations.literal: The ministers requested that the capital be moved to Chang'an. Bobo said: "Do I not know that Chang'an has been the capital of emperors through the ages, rich and securely fortified!
translations.idiomatic: The ministers asked that the capital be moved to Chang'an. Bobo said, "Do I not know that Chang'an has been the seat of emperors through the ages, fertile and strongly fortified!

sentences.zh: 然晉人僻遠，終不能為吾患。

translations.literal: Yet the Jin people are remote and out of the way—they can never become my trouble.
translations.idiomatic: But the Jin people are distant and remote—they can never truly threaten me.

sentences.zh: 魏與我風俗略同，土壤鄰接，自統萬距魏境裁百餘里，朕在長安，統萬必危；

translations.literal: Wei and I are roughly alike in custom, and our lands border each other; from Tongwan to the Wei frontier is only a little over a hundred li—if I am in Chang'an, Tongwan will surely be in danger;
translations.idiomatic: Wei and I are close in custom and our territories adjoin; from Tongwan to the Wei border is barely a hundred li more—if I stay in Chang'an, Tongwan will be in peril;

sentences.zh: 若在統萬，魏必不敢濟河而西。

translations.literal: If I stay at Tongwan, Wei will surely not dare cross the river and advance west.
translations.idiomatic: If I remain at Tongwan, Wei will not dare cross the river and march west.

sentences.zh: 諸卿適未見此耳。

translations.literal: You gentlemen simply have not seen this.
translations.idiomatic: You simply have not seen this.

sentences.zh: 」皆曰：「非所及也。

translations.literal: " All said: "This is beyond us.
translations.idiomatic: " All said, "That is beyond us.

sentences.zh: 」乃於長安置南台，以赫連瑰領大將軍、雍州牧、錄南台尚書事；

translations.literal: " He then established the Southern Platform at Chang'an, with Helian Gui as Grand General, Governor of Yong Province, and recorder of affairs of the Southern Platform Masters of Writing;
translations.idiomatic: " He then set up the Southern Platform at Chang'an, appointing Helian Gui Grand General, Governor of Yong Province, and recorder of Southern Platform secretariat affairs;

sentences.zh: 勃勃還統萬，大赦，改元真興。

translations.literal: Bobo returned to Tongwan, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Zhenxing.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo returned to Tongwan, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Zhenxing.

sentences.zh: 勃勃性驕虐，視民如草芥。

translations.literal: Bobo was by nature arrogant and cruel, treating the people like grass and chaff.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo was by nature arrogant and brutal, treating the people like weeds.

sentences.zh: 常居城上，置弓劍於側，有所嫌忿，手自殺之。

translations.literal: He constantly lived atop the city wall, with bow and sword at his side; whenever he felt resentment, he killed the person with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: He often lived atop the city wall with bow and sword at hand, and whenever he took offense he killed the person himself.

sentences.zh: 群臣迕視者鑿其目，笑者決其脣，諫者先截其舌而後斬之。

translations.literal: Those among the ministers who looked at him wrong had their eyes gouged out; those who laughed had their lips cut off; those who remonstrated had their tongues cut off first and then were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers who looked at him the wrong way had their eyes gouged out; those who laughed had their lips slit; those who remonstrated had their tongues cut out first and were then beheaded.

sentences.zh: 初，司馬楚之奉其父榮期之喪歸建康，會宋公裕誅剪宗室之有才望者，楚之叔父宣期、兄貞之皆死，楚之亡匿竟陵蠻中。

translations.literal: Earlier, Sima Chuzhi was returning to Jiankang for his father Rongqi's funeral when Duke Yu of Song was executing talented and influential members of the imperial clan; Chuzhi's uncle Xuanqi and elder brother Zhenzhi both died, and Chuzhi fled and hid among the Man tribes of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Sima Chuzhi was escorting his father Rongqi's coffin back to Jiankang when Duke Yu of Song began killing talented and prominent members of the imperial house. Chuzhi's uncle Xuanqi and elder brother Zhenzhi both died, and Chuzhi fled into hiding among the Man tribes of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 及從祖休之自江陵奔秦，楚之亡之汝、穎間，聚眾以謀復仇。

translations.literal: When his distant cousin Xiuzhi fled from Jiangling to Qin, Chuzhi went into the region between Ru and Ying, gathered followers, and plotted revenge.
translations.idiomatic: When his kinsman Xiuzhi fled from Jiangling to Qin, Chuzhi made for the Ru-Ying region, gathered followers, and plotted revenge.

sentences.zh: 楚之少有英氣，能折節下士，有眾萬餘，屯據長社。

translations.literal: Chuzhi had valor from youth, could humble himself before scholars, had more than ten thousand followers, and encamped at Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi had been spirited from youth, knew how to defer to men of talent, commanded more than ten thousand followers, and held Changshe.

sentences.zh: 裕使刺客沐謙往刺之，楚之待謙甚厚。

translations.literal: Yu sent the assassin Mu Qian to stab him; Chuzhi treated Qian with great generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent the assassin Mu Qian to kill him, but Chuzhi treated Qian with great kindness.

sentences.zh: 謙欲發，未得間，乃夜稱疾，知楚之必往問疾，因欲刺之。

translations.literal: Qian wished to strike but found no opening; he then feigned illness by night, knowing Chuzhi would surely come to inquire after his health, and intended to stab him then.
translations.idiomatic: Qian meant to strike but found no chance. That night he pretended to be ill, knowing Chuzhi would come to visit him, and planned to kill him then.

sentences.zh: 楚之果自繼湯藥往視疾，情意勤篤，謙不忍發，乃出匕首於席下，以狀告之曰：「將軍深為劉裕所忌，願勿輕率以自保全。

translations.literal: Chuzhi indeed personally brought medicine and went to visit his sickbed with earnest care; Qian could not bear to strike, but drew the dagger from beneath the mat, told him the truth, and said: "The General is deeply envied by Liu Yu—please do not act rashly and fail to preserve yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi indeed came in person with medicine and nursed him with devoted care. Qian could not bring himself to strike. He drew the dagger from beneath the mat, confessed the plot, and said, "The General is deeply feared by Liu Yu—please do not act rashly and risk your life.

sentences.zh: 」遂委身事之，為之防衛。

translations.literal: " He then gave himself over to serve Chuzhi and became his bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: " He then entered Chuzhi's service and became his bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 王鎮惡之死也，沈田子殺其兄弟七人，唯弟康得免，逃就宋公裕於彭城，裕以為相國行參軍。

translations.literal: When Wang Zhen'e died, Shen Tianzi killed seven of his brothers; only his younger brother Kang escaped, fled to Duke Yu of Song at Pengcheng, and Yu made him Acting Secretary to the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhen'e died, Shen Tianzi killed seven of his brothers. Only the younger brother Kang escaped, fled to Duke Yu of Song at Pengcheng, and was made Acting Secretary to the Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 康求還洛陽視母；

translations.literal: Kang requested to return to Luoyang to see his mother;
translations.idiomatic: Kang asked to return to Luoyang to see his mother;

sentences.zh: 會長安不守，康糾合關中徙民，得百許人，驅帥僑戶七百餘家，共保金墉城。

translations.literal: When Chang'an fell, Kang rallied transplanted people from Guanzhong, gathered about a hundred men, and drove to lead more than seven hundred migrant households in jointly defending Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang'an fell, Kang gathered displaced people from Guanzhong, mustered about a hundred men, and led more than seven hundred migrant households in holding Jincheng together.

sentences.zh: 時宗室多逃亡在河南，有司馬文榮者，帥乞活千餘戶屯金墉城南；

translations.literal: At that time many of the imperial clan had fled to Henan; there was one Sima Wenrong, who led more than a thousand Qihuo households encamped south of Jincheng;
translations.idiomatic: Many members of the imperial clan had fled into Henan at the time. Sima Wenrong led more than a thousand Qihuo households and encamped south of Jincheng;

sentences.zh: 又有司馬道恭，自東垣帥三千人屯城西，司馬順明帥五千人屯陵雲台，司馬楚之屯柏谷塢。

translations.literal: Also Sima Daogong, from Dongyuan, led three thousand men encamped west of the city; Sima Shunming led five thousand men encamped at Lingyun Terrace; Sima Chuzhi encamped at Baigu Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Daogong came from Dongyuan with three thousand men and encamped west of the city; Sima Shunming led five thousand men at Lingyun Terrace; Sima Chuzhi held Baigu Stockade.

sentences.zh: 魏河內鎮將於栗磾游騎在芒山上，攻逼交至，康堅守六旬。

translations.literal: Wei General of the Interior Garrison Yu Libo had roaming cavalry on Mount Mang; attacks and pressings came one after another, and Kang held firm for sixty days.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Libo, the Wei garrison commander of Henei, sent roaming cavalry onto Mount Mang. Attacks came in waves, and Kang held out for sixty days.

sentences.zh: 裕以康為河東太守，遣兵救之，平等皆散走。

translations.literal: Yu made Kang Administrator of Hedong and sent troops to rescue him; Ping et al. all scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yu appointed Kang Administrator of Hedong and sent troops to relieve him; Ping and the others all broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 康勸課農桑，百姓甚親賴之。

translations.literal: Kang urged and supervised agriculture and sericulture; the people came to rely on him with great affection.
translations.idiomatic: Kang encouraged farming and sericulture, and the people came to trust and depend on him.

sentences.zh: 司馬順明、司馬道恭及平陽太守薛辯皆降於魏，魏以辯為河東太守以拒夏人。

translations.literal: Sima Shunming, Sima Daogong, and Administrator of Pingyang Xue Bian all surrendered to Wei; Wei made Bian Administrator of Hedong to resist the Xia people.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shunming, Sima Daogong, and Pingyang Administrator Xue Bian all surrendered to Wei. Wei appointed Bian Administrator of Hedong to hold the Xia forces at bay.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，秦征西將軍孔子帥騎五千討吐谷渾覓地於弱水南，大破之，覓地帥其眾六千降於夏，拜弱水護軍。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Qin Western Campaigning General Kongzi led five thousand cavalry to attack Murong Midi of Tuyuhun south of the Ruoshui, defeated him thoroughly, Midi led his six thousand followers in surrendering to Xia, and was appointed Protector-General of Ruoshui.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Western Qin Western Campaigning General Kongzi led five thousand cavalry against Tuyuhun's Midi south of the Ruoshui, routed him, and Midi led six thousand followers in surrender to Xia, where he was made Protector-General of Ruoshui.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，魏主嗣有事於東廟，助祭者數百國；

translations.literal: On day gengchen, the Wei ruler Si performed rites at the Eastern Temple; nations assisting in sacrifice numbered in the hundreds;
translations.idiomatic: On day gengchen, Wei ruler Si performed rites at the Eastern Temple, with hundreds of states sending envoys to assist in the sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 辛巳，南巡至雁門。

translations.literal: On day xinsi, he toured south as far as Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: On day xinsi, he toured south as far as Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 五月，庚寅朔，魏主嗣觀漁於灅水。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on gengyin the first day of the month, the Wei ruler Si watched fishing at the Lei River.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on gengyin the first day of the month, Wei ruler Si watched fishing on the Lei River.

sentences.zh: 己亥，還平城。

translations.literal: On day jihai, he returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On day jihai, he returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 涼公歆用刑過嚴，又好治宮室。

translations.literal: Duke of Liang Xin employed punishments that were excessively harsh and also loved to build palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Liang Xin punished too harshly and also loved to build palaces.

sentences.zh: 從事中郎張顯上疏，以為：「涼土三分，勢不支久。

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman Zhang Xian submitted a memorial, saying: "The Liang territory is divided three ways; this situation cannot last long.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Gentleman Zhang Xian submitted a memorial saying, "The Liang lands are divided three ways and cannot long endure.

sentences.zh: 兼併之本，在於務農；

translations.literal: The foundation of annexation lies in devoting effort to agriculture;
translations.idiomatic: The basis of conquest lies in putting agriculture first;

sentences.zh: 懷遠之略，莫如寬簡。

translations.literal: The strategy for winning distant peoples is nothing so good as leniency and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: The best policy for winning distant peoples is leniency and simplicity.

sentences.zh: 今入歲已來，陰陽失序，風雨乖和；

translations.literal: Since this year began, yin and yang have lost their proper order, wind and rain have been out of harmony;
translations.idiomatic: Since the year began, yin and yang have fallen out of order and wind and rain have been unseasonable;

sentences.zh: 是宜減膳撤懸，側身修道，而更繁刑峻法，繕築不止，殆非所以致興隆也。

translations.literal: At such a time one should reduce meals and remove hanging bells, and cultivate the Way with humble self-reform—yet instead you increase harsh laws and never cease building; this is hardly the way to bring prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: This is the time to eat sparingly, remove music, and reform yourself in humility—yet you impose harsher punishments and never stop building. That is hardly the way to secure prosperity.

sentences.zh: 昔文王以百里而興，二世以四海而滅，前車之軌，得失昭然。

translations.literal: In antiquity King Wen rose with only a hundred li, while the Second Emperor perished though he held the four seas—the tracks of the overturned cart ahead make gain and loss clear.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen rose from a domain of a hundred li, while the Second Emperor lost the realm though he held the four seas—the overturned cart ahead shows plainly what succeeds and what fails.

sentences.zh: 太祖以神聖之姿，為西夏所推，左取酒泉，右開西域。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor, with his sacred and numinous presence, was pushed forward by Western Xia; he took Jiuquan on the left and opened the Western Regions on the right.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor, in his sacred majesty, was raised up by Western Xia; he seized Jiuquan and opened the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 殿下不能奉承遺志，混壹涼土，侔蹤張後，將何以下見先王乎！

translations.literal: Your Highness cannot carry on his testamentary will, unify the Liang lands, and match the footprints of Zhang Hou—how then will you face the former king below!
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness has not carried on his legacy, unified the Liang domain, or matched the achievements of Zhang Hou—how will you face the former king in the afterlife!

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜，胡夷之傑，內修政事，外禮英賢，攻戰之際，身先士卒，百姓懷之，樂為之用。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengsun, outstanding among the Hu and Yi peoples, cultivated governance within and honored worthies without; in battle he took the lead before his soldiers; the people hold him in regard and gladly serve him.
