translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengsun, a leader among the Hu and Yi, governs well at home and honors worthy men abroad; in battle he leads from the front, and the people esteem him and serve him willingly.

sentences.zh: 臣謂殿下非但不能平殄蒙遜，亦懼蒙遜方為社稷之憂。

translations.literal: Your servant says Your Highness will not only be unable to pacify and exterminate Mengsun, but I also fear Mengsun will become the state's great worry.
translations.idiomatic: I fear Your Highness will not only fail to pacify and destroy Mengsun, but that Mengsun will become a grave threat to the state itself.

sentences.zh: 」歆覽之，不悅。

translations.literal: " When Xin read it, he was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " Xin read it and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 主簿汜稱上疏諫曰：「天之子愛人主，殷勤至矣；

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Si Cheng submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying: "The Son of Heaven loves the ruler, His solicitude reaching the utmost;
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Si Cheng submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "The Son of Heaven loves the sovereign with the utmost solicitude;

sentences.zh: 故政之不修，下災異以戒告之，改者雖危必昌，不改者雖安必亡。

translations.literal: therefore when governance is not cultivated, He sends down disasters and anomalies to warn and admonish; those who change, though in peril, will surely prosper; those who do not change, though secure, will surely perish.
translations.idiomatic: so when governance is neglected, Heaven sends disasters and omens as warnings—those who reform, though endangered, will flourish; those who do not, though secure, will perish.

sentences.zh: 元年三月癸卯，敦煌謙德堂陷；

translations.literal: In the first year, third month, day guimao, the Humble Virtue Hall at Dunhuang collapsed;
translations.idiomatic: In year one, third month, on day guimao, the Humble Virtue Hall at Dunhuang collapsed;

sentences.zh: 八月，效穀地裂；

translations.literal: in the eighth month, the ground split at Xiaogu;
translations.idiomatic: in the eighth month, the earth split open at Xiaogu;

sentences.zh: 二年元日，昏霧四塞；

translations.literal: on New Year's Day of the second year, murky fog blocked all four sides;
translations.idiomatic: on New Year's Day of the second year, murky fog sealed the land on every side;

sentences.zh: 四月，日赤無光，二旬乃復；

translations.literal: in the fourth month, the sun turned red and lost its light, and only after twenty days did it return;
translations.idiomatic: in the fourth month, the sun turned blood-red and dimmed, and did not recover for twenty days;

sentences.zh: 十一月，狐上南門；

translations.literal: in the eleventh month, a fox climbed the southern gate;
translations.idiomatic: in the eleventh month, a fox scaled the southern gate;

sentences.zh: 今茲春、夏，地頻五震；

translations.literal: this spring and summer, the earth shook five times in succession;
translations.idiomatic: this spring and summer, the earth shook five times;

sentences.zh: 六月，隕星於建康。

translations.literal: in the sixth month, a falling star at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: in the sixth month, a meteor fell at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 臣雖學不稽古，行年五十有九，請為殿下略言耳目之所聞見，不復能遠論書傳之事也。

translations.literal: Your servant, though my learning does not reach back to antiquity, having lived fifty-nine years, asks to speak briefly to Your Highness of what I have heard and seen with my own eyes and ears, and can no longer discuss matters far off in books and records.
translations.idiomatic: Though my learning does not reach deep into antiquity, I am fifty-nine years old, and I would speak briefly to Your Highness of what I have witnessed with my own eyes and ears—I cannot discourse on what lies distant in books and chronicles.

sentences.zh: 乃者鹹安之初，西平地裂，狐入謙光殿前；

translations.literal: recently, at the beginning of Xian'an, the ground split in Xiping, and a fox entered before the Humble Radiance Hall;
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago, at the start of the Xian'an era, the earth split open at Xiping and a fox entered the forecourt of the Humble Radiance Hall;

sentences.zh: 俄而秦師奄至，都城不守。

translations.literal: soon after, Qin forces arrived suddenly, and the capital could not be held.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Qin armies swept in, and the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 梁熙既為涼州，不撫百姓，專為聚斂，建元十九年，姑臧南門崩，隕石於閒豫堂；

translations.literal: After Liang Xi became governor of Liang Province, he did not comfort the people but devoted himself solely to accumulation and extraction; in the nineteenth year of Jianyuan, the southern gate of Guzang collapsed, and a stone fell at the Leisure and Ease Hall;
translations.idiomatic: Once Liang Xi took Liang Province, he neglected the people and devoted himself only to extraction; in the nineteenth year of Jianyuan, Guzang's southern gate collapsed and a meteorite struck the Leisure and Ease Hall;

sentences.zh: 明年為呂光所殺。

translations.literal: the next year he was killed by Lü Guang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Lü Guang killed him.

sentences.zh: 段業稱制此方，三年之中，地震五十餘所；

translations.literal: when Duan Ye claimed sovereignty in this region, within three years there were earthquakes at more than fifty places;
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Ye claimed rule over this region, more than fifty earthquakes struck within three years;

sentences.zh: 既而先王龍興於瓜州，蒙遜篡弒於張掖。

translations.literal: soon after, the former king arose like a dragon at Guazhou, and Mengsun usurped and murdered at Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: Then the former king rose to power at Guazhou, and Mengsun seized the throne by murder at Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 此皆目前之成事，殿下所明知也。

translations.literal: these are all accomplished facts before our eyes, which Your Highness knows clearly.
translations.idiomatic: These are recent events that Your Highness knows full well.

sentences.zh: 效穀，先王鴻漸之地；

translations.literal: Xiaogu is the place where the former king first made his gradual ascent;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogu is where the former king first began his rise;

sentences.zh: 謙德，即尊之室；

translations.literal: Humble Virtue is the chamber of immediate honor;
translations.idiomatic: Humble Virtue is Your Highness's own hall of honor;

sentences.zh: 基陷地裂，大凶之征也。

translations.literal: foundations collapsing and earth splitting—these are great signs of ill fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Collapsed foundations and riven earth are grave omens of calamity.

sentences.zh: 日者，太陽之精，中國之象；

translations.literal: the sun is the essence of the Great Yang, the emblem of the Central State;
translations.idiomatic: The sun is the essence of the Great Yang, the symbol of the civilized center;

sentences.zh: 赤而無光，中國將衰。

translations.literal: red yet without light—the Central State will decline.
translations.idiomatic: Blood-red and dim—the civilized realm will wane.

sentences.zh: 諺曰：『野獸入家，主人將去。

translations.literal: a proverb says: "When wild beasts enter the home, the master is about to depart.
translations.idiomatic: As the proverb says: "When wild beasts enter the house, the master is about to leave.

sentences.zh: 』狐上南門，亦變異之大者也。

translations.literal: " A fox climbing the southern gate is also among the greatest of strange transformations.
translations.idiomatic: " A fox scaling the southern gate is among the gravest of portents.

sentences.zh: 今蠻夷益盛，中國益微。

translations.literal: now the barbarians grow ever stronger, and the Central State grows ever weaker.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian power grows while the civilized realm weakens.

sentences.zh: 願殿下亟罷宮室之役，止游畋之娛，延禮英俊，愛養百姓，以應天變，防未然。

translations.literal: I wish Your Highness would urgently cease palace-building labors, stop the diversions of hunting excursions, extend courtesy to worthy talents, cherish and nurture the people, thereby responding to Heaven's changes and guarding against what has not yet happened.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Highness to halt palace construction at once, abandon the pleasures of the hunt, honor men of talent, cherish the people, respond to Heaven's warnings, and forestall disaster before it comes.

sentences.zh: 」歆不從。

translations.literal: " Xin did not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Xin refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，宋公裕始受進爵之命。

translations.literal: autumn, seventh month, Duke Yu of Song first received the command of promotion in rank.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Duke Yu of Song first received orders promoting his rank.

sentences.zh: 八月，移鎮壽陽，以度支尚書劉懷慎為督淮北諸軍事、徐州刺史，鎮彭城。

translations.literal: in the eighth month, he transferred his headquarters to Shouyang, and made Revenue Minister Liu Huaishen Superintendent of all military affairs north of the Huai River and Inspector of Xuzhou, stationed at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he moved his headquarters to Shouyang and appointed Revenue Minister Liu Huaishen to oversee all military affairs north of the Huai and serve as Inspector of Xuzhou, stationed at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 辛未，魏主嗣東巡；

translations.literal: on day xinwei, the Wei ruler Si toured east;
translations.idiomatic: On day xinwei, Wei ruler Si toured the east;

sentences.zh: 甲申，還平城。

translations.literal: on day jiashen, he returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On day jiashen, he returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 九月，宋王裕自解揚州牧。

translations.literal: in the ninth month, Prince Yu of Song resigned from his post as Governor of Yang Province on his own initiative.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Prince Yu of Song relinquished his post as Governor of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 秦左衛將軍匹達等將兵討彭利和於漒川，大破之，利和單騎奔仇池；

translations.literal: Qin's Left Guard General Pi Da and others led troops to attack Peng Lihe at Qiangchuan, routed him greatly, and Lihe fled alone on horseback to Chouchi;
translations.idiomatic: Qin Left Guard General Pi Da and others marched against Peng Lihe at Qiangchuan, defeated him utterly, and Lihe fled alone on horseback to Chouchi;

sentences.zh: 獲其妻子，徙羌豪三千戶於枹罕，漒川羌三萬餘戶皆安堵如故。

translations.literal: they captured his wife and children, relocated three thousand Qiang noble households to Baohan, and the more than thirty thousand Qiang households of Qiangchuan all remained settled as before.
translations.idiomatic: They captured his wife and children, relocated three thousand leading Qiang households to Baohan, and the more than thirty thousand Qiang households of Qiangchuan resumed their lives undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，以尚書右僕射王松壽為益州刺史，鎮漒川。

translations.literal: winter, tenth month, Wang Songsou, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Inspector of Yizhou and stationed at Qiangchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Songsou was appointed Inspector of Yizhou and stationed at Qiangchuan.

sentences.zh: 宋王裕以河南蕭條，乙酉，徙司州刺史義真為揚州刺史，鎮石頭，蕭太紀謂裕曰：「道憐汝布衣兄弟，宜用為揚州。

translations.literal: Prince Yu of Song, because Henan was desolate and empty, on day yiyou transferred Inspector of Sizhou Yizhen to be Inspector of Yang Province, stationed at Shitou; Consort Dowager Xiao said to Yu: "Daolian is your brother of common-cloth days—you should use him for Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Because Henan lay wasted, Prince Yu of Song on day yiyou transferred Yizhen, Inspector of Sizhou, to Inspector of Yang Province at Shitou. Consort Dowager Xiao said to Yu, "Daolian is the brother who shared your humble days—you ought to give him Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 」裕曰：「寄奴於道憐，豈有所惜！

translations.literal: " Yu said: "Would Jinu begrudge Daolian anything!
translations.idiomatic: " Yu replied, "Would Jinu begrudge Daolian anything!

sentences.zh: 揚州根本所寄，事務至多，非道憐所了。

translations.literal: Yang Province is where the root of all rests; affairs are exceedingly many—not something Daolian can manage.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Province is the foundation of our power; its affairs are far too numerous for Daolian to manage.

sentences.zh: 」太妃曰：「道憐年出五十，豈不如汝十歲兒邪？

translations.literal: " The Consort Dowager said: "Daolian is past fifty—is he really not the equal of your ten-year-old son?
translations.idiomatic: " The Consort Dowager pressed, "Daolian is past fifty—is he truly less capable than your ten-year-old son?

sentences.zh: 」裕曰：「義真雖為刺史，事無大小，悉由寄奴。

translations.literal: " Yu said: "Though Yizhen holds the post of inspector, matters great and small all depend on Jinu.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu answered, "Though Yizhen holds the title of inspector, every matter, great or small, rests with Jinu.

sentences.zh: 道憐年長，不親其事，於聽望不足。

translations.literal: Daolian is older in years and would not personally attend to affairs—this would be insufficient for reputation among those who hear.
translations.idiomatic: Daolian is older and would not attend to affairs himself—it would harm our standing in the eyes of the court.

sentences.zh: 」太妃乃無言。

translations.literal: " The Consort Dowager then said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: " The Consort Dowager fell silent.

sentences.zh: 道憐性愚鄙而貪縱，故裕不肯用。

translations.literal: Daolian's nature was foolish and base, greedy and unrestrained, and therefore Yu refused to use him.
translations.idiomatic: Daolian was coarse, foolish, greedy, and unrestrained—so Yu would not appoint him.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁亥朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: eleventh month, first day of the month dinghai, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the first day dinghai, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 十二月，癸亥，魏主嗣西巡至雲中，從君子津西渡河，大獵於薛林山。

translations.literal: twelfth month, day guihai, the Wei ruler Si toured west as far as Yunzhong, crossed the river west from Junzi Ford, and hunted greatly at Mt. Xuelin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on day guihai, Wei ruler Si toured west to Yunzhong, crossed the Yellow River west of Junzi Ford, and hunted extensively on Mt. Xuelin.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，宋王裕加殊禮，進王太妃為太后，世子為太子。

translations.literal: on day xinmao, Prince Yu of Song was granted extraordinary honors; the prince's consort dowager was advanced to empress dowager, and the heir was made crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On day xinmao, Prince Yu of Song was granted extraordinary honors: his consort dowager was elevated to empress dowager, and his heir was named crown prince.

translations.idiomatic: Category: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
